paragraphs.fa: ﴿ بنام گوينده توانا ﴾
paragraphs.translit: ba-nām-i gūyanda-yi tavānā.

i18n.en: In the name of the Almighty Speaker.

notes.official: The Persian series opens with a different invocation from the Arabic. *ba-nām-i gūyanda-yi tavānā*, 'In the name of the Almighty Speaker' (*gūyanda*, the active participle of *guftan* 'to speak'), foregrounds divine *speech* where Part I's heading (*huwa l-bahiyyu l-abhā*) turned on the *b-h-y* 'glory' root — apt for a book whose aphorisms are cast as the direct first-person utterance of the 'Friend.' Rendered by the lexical core; no divergence.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای صاحبان هوش و گوش ﴾ اوّل سروش دوست اينست ای بلبل معنوی جز در گلبن معانی جای مگزين و ای هدهد سليمان عشق جز در سبای جانان وطن مگير و ای عنقای بقا جز در قاف وفا محلّ مپذير * اينست مکان تو اگر بلامکان بپر جان برپری و آهنگ مقام خود رايگان نمائی *
paragraphs.translit: ay ṣāḥibān-i hūsh u gūsh! avval-i surūsh-i dūst īnast: ay bulbul-i maʿnavī, juz dar gulbun-i maʿānī jāy magzīn; va ay hudhud-i sulaymān-i ʿishq, juz dar sabā-yi jānān vaṭan magīr; va ay ʿanqā-yi baqā, juz dar qāf-i vafā maḥall mapaẕīr. īnast makān-i tu; agar bi-lā-makān bi-parī jān bar-parī va āhang-i maqām-i khud rāyagān namāʾī.

i18n.en: O ye that possess wit and ear! The first tiding of the Friend is this: O spiritual nightingale, take not thine abode save in the rose-bower of inner meanings; and O hoopoe of the Solomon of love, seek no homeland save in the Sheba of the Beloved; and O phoenix of eternity, choose no dwelling-place save upon the Qáf of faithfulness. This is thy station. Wouldst thou wing thy flight with the soul unto the Placeless, then soar, and set thy course toward thine own station freely.

notes.official: The opening aphorism stacks the fixed menagerie of the Persian lyric-Sufi register. *bulbul* ('nightingale'), *gul* / *gulbun* ('rose' / 'rose-bower'), and *hudhud* ('hoopoe') are rendered by their English glosses; the named entities are retained as proper names — *Qáf* (the world-encircling cosmic mountain) and, through the Solomon errand, *Sabā* ('Sheba,' the hoopoe's mission in Qur'an 27:20-44). *ʿanqā* — the mythic bird that dwells upon Qáf — is rendered 'phoenix,' its nearest English analogue, and is kept lexically distinct from *humā* (HWP-38). These images carry a settled valence in ʿAṭṭār's *Manṭiq al-ṭayr* and in Ḥāfiẓ; the retain-vs-gloss policy is fixed in the overlay bestiary entry. *lā-makān* ('the Placeless,' the realm beyond spatial location) is rendered 'the Placeless' throughout the Part.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر روح ﴾ هر طيری را نظر بر آشيان است و هر بلبلی را مقصود جمال گل مگر طيور افئده عباد که بتراب فانی قانع شده از آشيان باقی دور مانده‌اند و بگِلهای بعد توجّه نموده از گُلهای قرب محروم گشته‌اند * زهی حيرت و حسرت و افسوس و دريغ که بابريقی از امواج بحر رفيق اعلی گذشته‌اند و از افق ابهی دور مانده‌اند *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i rūḥ! har ṭayrī rā naẓar bar āshiyān ast va har bulbulī rā maqṣūd jamāl-i gul; magar ṭuyūr-i afʾida-yi ʿibād ki bi-turāb-i fānī qāniʿ shuda az āshiyān-i bāqī dūr mānda-and va bi-gil-hā-yi buʿd tavajjuh namūda az gul-hā-yi qurb maḥrūm gashta-and. zih-i ḥayrat u ḥasrat u afsūs u darīgh ki bi-ibrīqī az amvāj-i baḥr-i rafīq-i aʿlā guẕashta-and va az ufuq-i abhā dūr mānda-and.

i18n.en: O Son of the Spirit! Every bird hath its gaze upon its nest, and every nightingale its aim in the beauty of the rose — save the birds of the hearts of [My] servants, who, content with perishable dust, have strayed far from the abiding nest, and, having turned toward the mires of remoteness, have been deprived of the roses of nearness. What wonder and regret, what sorrow and pity, that for a single ewer[-full] they have passed by the waves of the ocean of the All-Highest Companion, and remained far from the Most Glorious Horizon.

notes.official: Two features. First, the deliberate minimal-pair wordplay *gul* / *gil*: the servants have turned toward the *gil-hā* ('mires,' گِل) of remoteness and been deprived of the *gul-hā* ('roses,' گُل) of nearness — two words distinguished in the vocalized text only by the vowel (*u* / *i*). The rendering 'mires of remoteness … roses of nearness' preserves the paired contrast. Second, *ufuq-i abhā* ('the Most Glorious Horizon'): *abhā* is the elative of *bahiyy* (√b-h-y), the root of the author's title *Bahāʾ-Allāh*. Consistent with the ratified Part I treatment, the surface English keeps the neutral 'Most Glorious'; the onomastic resonance is recorded here as lexical fact and is not foregrounded. The *turāb* / *khāk* dust-vocabulary (*turāb-i fānī*, 'perishable dust') is levelled to 'dust' per the vocative entry.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای دوست﴾ در روضه قلب جز گل عشق مکار و از ذيل بلبل حبّ و شوق دست مدار * مصاحبت ابرار را غنيمت دان و از مرافقت اشرار دست و دل هر دو بردار *
paragraphs.translit: ay dūst! dar rawḍa-yi qalb juz gul-i ʿishq makār va az ẕayl-i bulbul-i ḥubb u shawq dast madār. muṣāḥabat-i abrār rā ghanīmat dān va az murāfaqat-i ashrār dast u dil har du bardār.

i18n.en: O Friend! In the garden of thy heart plant naught but the rose of love, and from the nightingale of affection and longing loose not thy hold. Prize the companionship of the righteous, and from fellowship with the wicked withdraw both hand and heart.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر انصاف ﴾ کدام عاشق كه جز در وطن معشوق محلّ گيرد و کدام طالب که بی مطلوب راحت جويد ؟ عاشق صادق را حيات در وصال است و موت در فراق * صدرشان از صبر خالی و قلوبشان از اصطبار مقدّس از صد هزار جان درگذرند و بکوی جانان شتابند *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i inṣāf! kudām ʿāshiq ki juz dar vaṭan-i maʿshūq maḥall gīrad va kudām ṭālib ki bī maṭlūb rāḥat jūyad? ʿāshiq-i ṣādiq rā ḥayāt dar viṣāl ast va mawt dar firāq. ṣadr-ishān az ṣabr khālī va qulūb-ishān az iṣṭibār muqaddas; az ṣad hazār jān dar-guẕarand va bi-kūy-i jānān shitāband.

i18n.en: O Son of Equity! What lover is there who would take his abode anywhere save in the homeland of the beloved, and what seeker who would seek rest without the sought-for? To the true lover, life lieth in reunion and death in separation. Their breasts are void of patience and their hearts hallowed above forbearance; they pass beyond a hundred thousand lives and hasten to the quarter of the Beloved.

notes.official: *pisar-i inṣāf*, 'O Son of Equity.' *inṣāf* (√n-ṣ-f, 'to halve, divide evenly') is held to 'equity,' distinct from *ʿadl* 'justice,' per the equity/justice entry established in Part I; the same distinction governs the Persian vocative here and at HWP-77.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر خاک ﴾ براستی ميگويم غافلترين عباد کسی است که در قول مجادله نمايد و بر برادر خود تفوّق جويد * بگو ای برادران باعمال خود را بيارائيد نه باقوال *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i khāk! bi-rāstī mī-gūyam: ghāfil-tarīn-i ʿibād kasī ast ki dar qawl mujādala namāyad va bar birādar-i khud tafavvuq jūyad. bi-gū: ay birādarān! bi-aʿmāl khud rā biyārāʾīd, na bi-aqvāl.

i18n.en: O Son of Dust! Verily I say: the most heedless of servants is he that wrangleth in words and seeketh to exalt himself above his brother. Say: O brethren! Adorn yourselves with deeds, not with words.

notes.official: First of the dust-vocatives: *pisar-i khāk*, 'O Son of Dust.' Persian *khāk* and the Arabic loan *turāb* both mean 'dust,' and both are levelled to 'Dust' as vocatives. Unlike the Part I *insān* / *bashar* pair — where two lexemes carried genuinely distinct semantic weights — *khāk* and *turāb* function here as interchangeable stylistic variants (see HWP-48, where the two stand in deliberate parallel: created *min turāb*, returning to *khāk*), so distinguishing them in English would manufacture a contrast the Persian does not mark. The distinct terms of the earth-field — *gil* 'mire/clay,' *ramād* 'ashes' (HWP-39) — are kept separate.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسران ارض ﴾ براستی بدانيد قلبی که در آن شائبه حسد باقی باشد البتّه بجبروت باقی من در نيايد و از ملکوت تقديس من روائح قدس نشنود *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisarān-i arḍ! bi-rāstī bidānīd: qalbī ki dar ān shāʾiba-yi ḥasad bāqī bāshad, al-batta bi-jabarūt-i bāqī-yi man dar-nayāyad va az malakūt-i taqdīs-i man ravāʾiḥ-i quds nashnavad.

i18n.en: O Sons of Earth! Know ye truly: a heart wherein there yet lingereth the least trace of envy shall never enter My everlasting realm of omnipotence, nor breathe the fragrances of holiness from the kingdom of My sanctity.

notes.official: *jabarūt-i bāqī-yi man* ('My everlasting realm of omnipotence,' *jabarūt*) and *malakūt-i taqdīs-i man* ('the kingdom of My sanctity,' *malakūt*) are named together; the realm-hierarchy mapping keeps them distinct — *jabarūt* 'realm of omnipotence,' *malakūt* 'kingdom,' *mulk* 'dominion' — where a looser rendering would collapse them. The heart harbouring 'the least trace of envy' (*shāʾiba-yi ḥasad*) is barred from both.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر حبّ ﴾ از تو تا رفرف امتناع قرب و سدره ارتفاع عشق قدمی فاصله قدم اوّل بردار و قدم ديگر بر عالم قدم گذار و در سرادق خلد وارد شو * پس بشنو آنچه از قلم عزّ نزول يافت *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i ḥubb! az tu tā rafraf-i imtināʿ-i qurb va sidra-yi irtifāʿ-i ʿishq qadamī fāṣila. qadam-i avval bardār va qadam-i dīgar bar ʿālam-i qidam guẕār va dar sarādiq-i khuld vārid shaw. pas bishnaw ānchi az qalam-i ʿizz nuzūl yāft.

i18n.en: O Son of Love! Between thee and the inaccessible height of nearness and the Lote-Tree of the loftiness of love there lieth but a single step. Take the first step, and with the other tread upon the realm of pre-eternity, and enter the pavilion of everlastingness. Hearken, then, unto that which hath descended from the Pen of glory.

notes.official: The wordplay *qadam* / *qidam*: 'take the first *qadam* (step), and with the other *qadam* (step) tread upon the *ʿālam-i qidam* (the realm of pre-eternity).' *qadam* (قدم, 'step, foot') and *qidam* (قِدَم, 'pre-eternity, beginninglessness' — the theological attribute opposed to *ḥudūth*, 'origination in time') share one consonantal skeleton and are divided only by vocalization. Rendered 'step … tread upon the realm of pre-eternity,' preserving the figure. *rafraf* and *sidra* (the Lote-Tree) belong to the miʿrāj vocabulary of Qur'an 53:14-16.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر عزّ ﴾ در سبيل قدس چالاک شو و بر افلاک انس قدم گذار قلب را بصيقل روح پاک کن و آهنگ ساحت لولاک نما *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i ʿizz! dar sabīl-i quds chālāk shaw va bar aflāk-i uns qadam guẕār; qalb rā bi-ṣayqal-i rūḥ pāk kun va āhang-i sāḥat-i lawlāk namā.

i18n.en: O Son of Glory! Be swift in the path of holiness, and set foot upon the heavens of fellowship. Cleanse thy heart with the burnish of the spirit, and set thy course toward the court of "but for thee."

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای سايه نابود ﴾ از مدارج ذلّ وهم بگذر و بمعارج عزّ يقين اندرا * چشم حق بگشا تا جمال مبين بينی و تبارک اللّه أحسن الخالقين گوئی*
paragraphs.translit: ay sāya-yi nābūd! az madārij-i ẕull-i vahm biguẕar va bi-maʿārij-i ʿizz-i yaqīn andar-ā. chashm-i ḥaqq bigushā tā jamāl-i mubīn bīnī va tabāraka llāhu aḥsanu l-khāliqīn gūʾī.

i18n.en: O Fleeting Shadow! Pass beyond the low stages of the abasement of vain fancy, and enter the lofty ascents of the glory of certitude. Open the eye of truth, that thou mayest behold the manifest Beauty and cry: "Blessed be God, the most excellent of Creators!"

notes.official: The verse closes with an embedded Qur'anic doxology: *tabāraka llāhu aḥsanu l-khāliqīn*, 'Blessed be God, the most excellent of Creators' (Qur'an 23:14). Rendered verbatim and retained in transliteration within the Arabic clause. *jamāl-i mubīn* ('the manifest Beauty') pairs *jamāl* with *mubīn* (√b-y-n).

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر هوی ﴾ براستی بشنو چشم فانی جمال باقی نشناسد و دل مرده جز بگُل پژمرده مشغول نشود زيرا که هر قرينی قرين خود را جويد و بجنس خود انس گيرد *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i havā! bi-rāstī bishnaw: chashm-i fānī jamāl-i bāqī nashnāsad va dil-i murda juz bi-gul-i pazhmurda mashghūl nashavad, zīrā ki har qarīnī qarīn-i khud rā jūyad va bi-jins-i khud uns gīrad.

i18n.en: O Son of Passion! Hearken truly: the perishing eye can never know the abiding Beauty, nor can the dead heart busy itself with aught but the withered rose; for every like seeketh its like and taketh intimacy with its own kind.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر تراب ﴾ کور شو تا جمالم بينی و کر شو تا لحن و صوت مليحم را شنوی و جاهل شو تا از علمم نصيب بری و فقير شو تا از بحر غنای لا يزالم قسمت بيزوال برداری * کور شو يعنی از مشاهده غير جمال من و کر شو يعنی از استماع کلام غير من و جاهل شو يعنی از سوای علم من تا با چشم پاک و دل طيّب و گوش لطيف بساحت قدسم درآئی *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i turāb! kūr shaw tā jamālam bīnī va kar shaw tā laḥn u ṣawt-i malīḥam rā shanavī va jāhil shaw tā az ʿilmam naṣīb barī va faqīr shaw tā az baḥr-i ghanā-yi lā-yazālam qismat-i bī-zavāl bardārī. kūr shaw yaʿnī az mushāhada-yi ghayr-i jamāl-i man, va kar shaw yaʿnī az istimāʿ-i kalām-i ghayr-i man, va jāhil shaw yaʿnī az sivā-yi ʿilm-i man, tā bā chashm-i pāk u dil-i ṭayyib u gūsh-i laṭīf bi-sāḥat-i qudsam dar-āʾī.

i18n.en: O Son of Dust! Be blind, that thou mayest behold My beauty; be deaf, that thou mayest hear My sweet melody and voice; be ignorant, that thou mayest partake of My knowledge; be poor, that thou mayest draw an unfailing portion from the ocean of My everlasting riches. Be blind — that is, to the beholding of any beauty save Mine; be deaf — that is, to the hearing of any word save Mine; be ignorant — that is, of all knowledge save Mine; that with pure eye and goodly heart and refined ear thou mayest enter the court of My holiness.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای صاحب دو چشم ﴾ چشمی بربند و چشمی برگشا * بربند يعنی از عالم و عالميان برگشا يعنی بجمال قدس جانان *
paragraphs.translit: ay ṣāḥib-i du chashm! chashmī bar-band va chashmī bar-gushā. bar-band yaʿnī az ʿālam u ʿālamiyān, bar-gushā yaʿnī bi-jamāl-i quds-i jānān.

i18n.en: O Possessor of Two Eyes! Close the one eye and open the other. Close the one — that is, to the world and to them that dwell therein; and open the other — to the hallowed beauty of the Beloved.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسران من ﴾ ترسم که از نغمه ورقاء فيض نبرده بديار فنا راجع شويد و جمال گُل نديده بآب و گِل باز گرديد *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisarān-i man! tarsam ki az naghma-yi varqāʾ fayḍ nabarda bi-diyār-i fanā rājiʿ shavīd va jamāl-i gul nadīda bi-āb u gil bāz gardīd.

i18n.en: O My Sons! I fear lest, having gained no grace from the song of the dove, ye return unto the abode of annihilation; and lest, never having beheld the beauty of the rose, ye go back unto water and clay.

notes.official: *varqāʾ* ('the dove') is rendered by its gloss, one of the glossed-not-retained bestiary decisions (overlay bestiary entry); here the *naghma-yi varqāʾ*, 'song of the dove,' is the call the addressee risks never hearing. The closing *āb u gil* ('water and clay') is the standard Persian figure for the base bodily creation of the human — the clay-and-water of Genesis 2:7 / Qur'an 15:26 — against which 'the beauty of the rose' stands.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای دوستان ﴾ بجمال فانی از جمال باقی مگذريد و بخاکدان ترابی دل مبنديد *
paragraphs.translit: ay dūstān! bi-jamāl-i fānī az jamāl-i bāqī maguẕarīd va bi-khākdān-i turābī dil mabandīd.

i18n.en: O Friends! Forsake not the abiding Beauty for a beauty that must perish, and set not your hearts upon this earthen heap of dust.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر روح ﴾ وقتی آيد که بلبل قدس معنوی از بيان اسرار معانی ممنوع شود و جميع از نغمه رحمانی و ندای سبحانی ممنوع گرديد*
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i rūḥ! vaqtī āyad ki bulbul-i quds-i maʿnavī az bayān-i asrār-i maʿānī mamnūʿ shavad va jamīʿ az naghma-yi raḥmānī va nidā-yi subḥānī mamnūʿ gardīd.

i18n.en: O Son of the Spirit! A time will come when the nightingale of holiness and inner meaning shall be forbidden to divulge the mysteries of meaning, and all shall be barred from the merciful melody and the glorious call.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای جوهر غفلت ﴾ دريغ که صد هزار لسان معنوی در لسانی ناطق و صد هزار معانی غيبی در لحنی ظاهر و لکن گوشی نه تا بشنود و قلبی نه تا حرفی بيابد *
paragraphs.translit: ay jawhar-i ghaflat! darīgh ki ṣad hazār lisān-i maʿnavī dar lisānī nāṭiq va ṣad hazār maʿānī-yi ghaybī dar laḥnī ẓāhir, va lākin gūshī na tā bishnavad va qalbī na tā ḥarfī biyābad.

i18n.en: O Essence of Heedlessness! Alas, a hundred thousand tongues of inner meaning speak in a single tongue, and a hundred thousand hidden meanings are made manifest in a single strain; yet there is no ear to hear, nor heart to grasp a single word.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای همگنان ﴾ ابواب لامکان باز گشته و ديار جانان از دم عاشقان زينت يافته و جميع از اين شهر روحانی محروم مانده‌اند الّا قليلی و از آن قليل هم با قلب طاهر و نفس مقدّس مشهود نگشت الّا اقلّ قليلی*
paragraphs.translit: ay hamganān! abvāb-i lā-makān bāz gashta va diyār-i jānān az dam-i ʿāshiqān zīnat yāfta, va jamīʿ az īn shahr-i rūḥānī maḥrūm mānda-and illā qalīlī, va az ān qalīl ham bā qalb-i ṭāhir u nafs-i muqaddas mashhūd nagasht illā aqall-i qalīlī.

i18n.en: O Comrades! The gates that open upon the Placeless are flung wide, and the country of the Beloved is adorned with the breath of lovers; yet all, save a few, have remained shut out from this spiritual city, and of that few, none was seen with pure heart and sanctified soul save the fewest of the few.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای اهل فردوس برين ﴾ اهل يقين را اخبار نمائيد که در فضای قدس قرب رضوان روضه جديدی ظاهر گشته و جميع اهل عالين و هياکل خلد برين طائف حول آن گشته‌اند * پس جهدی نمائيد تا بآن مقام درآئيد و حقائق اسرار عشق را از شقايقش جوئيد و جميع حکمتهای بالغه احديّه را از اثمار باقيه‌اش بيابيد * قرّت أبصار الّذين هم دخلوا فيه آمنين *
paragraphs.translit: ay ahl-i firdaws-i barīn! ahl-i yaqīn rā akhbār namāʾīd ki dar faḍā-yi quds-i qurb-i riḍvān rawḍa-yi jadīdī ẓāhir gashta va jamīʿ-i ahl-i ʿālīn u hayākil-i khuld-i barīn ṭāʾif ḥawl-i ān gashta-and. pas jahdī namāʾīd tā bi-ān maqām dar-āʾīd va ḥaqāʾiq-i asrār-i ʿishq rā az shaqāʾiqash jūyīd va jamīʿ-i ḥikmat-hā-yi bāligha-yi aḥadiyya rā az athmār-i bāqiya-ash biyābīd. qurrat abṣār alladhīna hum dakhalū fīhi āminīn.

i18n.en: O ye that dwell in the highest Paradise! Announce unto them that are assured: In the hallowed space of the nearness of Riḍván a new garden hath appeared, round which circle all the dwellers of the realms on high and the temples of the sublime paradise of eternity. Strive, then, to attain that station, and to seek out the realities of the mysteries of love from its anemones, and to gather all the consummate wisdoms of the Divine Oneness from its abiding fruits. Solaced are the eyes of them that have entered therein and abide in security.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای دوستان من ﴾ آيا فراموش کرده‌ايد آن صبح صادق روشنی را که در ظلّ شجره انيسا که در فردوس اعظم غرس شده جميع در آن فضای قدس مبارک نزد من حاضر بوديد ؟ و بسه کلمه طيّبه تکلّم فرمودم و جميع آن کلماترا شنيده و مدهوش گشتيد و آن کلمات اين بود * ای دوستان رضای خود را بر رضای من اختيار مکنيد و آنچه برای شما نخواهم هرگز مخواهيد و با دلهای مرده که بآمال و آرزو آلوده شده نزد من ميائيد * اگر صدر را مقدّس کنيد حال آن صحرا و آن فضا را بنظر در آريد و بيان من بر همه شما معلوم شود * (در سطر هشتم از اسطر قدس که در لوح پنجم از فردوس است ميفرمايد)
paragraphs.translit: ay dūstān-i man! āyā farāmūsh karda-īd ān ṣubḥ-i ṣādiq-i rawshanī rā ki dar ẓill-i shajara-yi anīsā ki dar firdaws-i aʿẓam ghars shuda jamīʿ dar ān faḍā-yi quds-i mubārak nazd-i man ḥāḍir būdīd? va bi-si kalima-yi ṭayyiba takallum farmūdam va jamīʿ-i ān kalimāt rā shanīda va madhūsh gashtīd, va ān kalimāt īn būd: ay dūstān! riḍā-yi khud rā bar riḍā-yi man ikhtiyār makunīd va ānchi barā-yi shumā nakhvāham hargiz makhvāhīd va bā dil-hā-yi murda ki bi-āmāl u ārzū ālūda shuda nazd-i man mayāʾīd. agar ṣadr rā muqaddas kunīd, ḥāl ān ṣaḥrā va ān faḍā rā bi-naẓar dar-ārīd va bayān-i man bar hama-yi shumā maʿlūm shavad. (dar saṭr-i hashtum az asṭur-i quds ki dar lawḥ-i panjum az firdaws ast mī-farmāyad.)

i18n.en: O My Friends! Have ye forgotten that true and radiant morn when, in the shade of the tree of companionship planted in the most great paradise, ye were all gathered before Me in that blessed and hallowed space? Three goodly words I spoke, and ye heard them all and were struck senseless; and those words were these: O Friends! Prefer not your own good-pleasure to My good-pleasure, and desire never that which I have not desired for you, and approach Me not with dead hearts defiled with hopes and cravings. Would ye but sanctify your breasts, ye would now call to mind that desert and that space, and My utterance would be made plain unto you all. (In the eighth line of the lines of holiness that are in the fifth Tablet of Paradise, He saith:)

notes.official: *shajara-yi anīsā*, 'the tree of companionship.' *anīsā* is read as an intensive-adjectival form of the root *uns* ('intimacy, sociability, companionship'; cf. *anīs* 'boon-companion'), qualifying the tree in the 'most great paradise' beneath which the covenant of the three words was made. A proper-name reading ('the Tree of Anísá') is possible but unattested; the Lote-Tree / Tree-of-Life register (*Sadratu'l-Muntahā*) is available but not forced into the surface text. Rendered adjectivally, 'the tree of companionship.'

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای مردگان فراش غفلت ﴾ قرنها گذشت و عمر گرانمايه را بانتها رسانده‌ايد و نَفَس پاکی از شما بساحت قدس ما نيامد * در ابحر شرک مستغرقيد و کلمه توحيد بر زبان ميرانيد * مبغوض مرا محبوب خود دانسته‌ايد و دشمن مرا دوست خود گرفته‌ايد و در ارض من بکمال خرمی و سرور مشی مينمائيد و غافل از آنکه زمين من از تو بيزار است و اشيای ارض از تو در گريز * اگر فی الجمله بصر بگشائی صد هزار حزن را از اين سرور خوشتر دانی و فنا را از اين حيات نيکوتر شمری *
paragraphs.translit: ay murdagān-i firāsh-i ghaflat! qarn-hā guẕasht va ʿumr-i girānmāya rā bi-intihā rasānda-īd va nafas-i pākī az shumā bi-sāḥat-i quds-i mā nayāmad. dar abḥur-i shirk mustaghraqīd va kalima-yi tawḥīd bar zabān mī-rānīd. mabghūḍ-i marā maḥbūb-i khud dānista-īd va dushman-i marā dūst-i khud girifta-īd va dar arḍ-i man bi-kamāl-i khurramī u surūr mashī mī-namāʾīd, va ghāfil az ānki zamīn-i man az tu bīzār ast va ashyā-yi arḍ az tu dar gurīz. agar fi l-jumla baṣar bigushāʾī, ṣad hazār ḥuzn rā az īn surūr khushtar dānī va fanā rā az īn ḥayāt nīkūtar shumarī.

i18n.en: O ye that lie as dead upon the couch of heedlessness! Ages have passed, and ye have brought your precious lives unto their end, yet not one pure breath hath ascended from you unto Our holy court. Ye are sunk in the seas of idolatry, yet ye let the word of the Divine Unity run upon your tongues. Ye have deemed My detested one your beloved, and have taken My enemy for your friend; and upon My earth ye walk in all gladness and joy, heedless that My earth is weary of you and that all things thereon flee from you. Wert thou but to open thine eye a little, thou wouldst reckon a hundred thousand sorrows sweeter than this joy, and wouldst count annihilation better than this life.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای خاک متحرّک ﴾ من بتو مأنوسم و تو از من مأيوس * سيف عصيان شجره اميد ترا بريده * و در جميع حال بتو نزديکم و تو در جميع احوال از من دور * و من عزّت بيزوال برای تو اختيار نمودم و تو ذلّت بی منتهی برای خود پسنديدی * آخر تا وقت باقی مانده رجوع کن و فرصت را مگذار *
paragraphs.translit: ay khāk-i mutaḥarrik! man bi-tu maʾnūsam va tu az man maʾyūs. sayf-i ʿiṣyān shajara-yi umīd-i turā burīda. va dar jamīʿ-i ḥāl bi-tu nazdīkam va tu dar jamīʿ-i aḥvāl az man dūr. va man ʿizzat-i bī-zavāl barā-yi tu ikhtiyār namūdam va tu ẕillat-i bī-muntahā barā-yi khud pasandīdī. ākhir tā vaqt bāqī mānda rujūʿ kun va furṣat rā maguẕār.

i18n.en: O Quickened Dust! I am intimate with thee, yet thou art despairing of Me. The sword of rebellion hath hewn down the tree of thy hope. At all times am I near unto thee, yet thou at all times art far from Me. Imperishable glory have I chosen for thee, yet boundless abasement hast thou chosen for thyself. Turn back, then, while yet there is time remaining, and let not the opportunity slip.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر هوی ﴾ اهل دانش و بينش سالها کوشيدند و بوصال ذی الجلال فائز نگشتند و عمرها دويدند و بلقای ذی الجمال نرسيدند * و تو نادويده بمنزل رسيده و ناطلبيده بمطلب واصل شدی * و بعد از جميع اين مقام و رتبه بحجاب نفس خود چنان محتجب ماندی که چشمت بجمال دوست نيفتاد و دستت بدامن يار نرسيد * فتعجّبوا من ذلک يا اولی الأبصار *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i havā! ahl-i dānish u bīnish sāl-hā kūshīdand va bi-viṣāl-i ẕi l-jalāl fāʾiz nagashtand va ʿumr-hā davīdand va bi-liqā-yi ẕi l-jamāl narasīdand. va tu nā-davīda bi-manzil rasīda va nā-ṭalabīda bi-maṭlab vāṣil shudī. va baʿd az jamīʿ-i īn maqām u rutba bi-ḥijāb-i nafs-i khud chunān muḥtajib māndī ki chashmat bi-jamāl-i dūst nayaftād va dastat bi-dāman-i yār narasīd. fa-taʿajjabū min ẕālika yā ulī l-abṣār.

i18n.en: O Son of Passion! The people of knowledge and insight have striven for years, yet attained not unto reunion with the Lord of Majesty; lifetimes have they run, yet reached not the presence of the Lord of Beauty. Yet thou, without running, hast reached the abode, and without seeking, hast attained the object of thy quest. And after all this rank and station, thou hast remained so veiled by the veil of thine own self that thine eye fell not upon the beauty of the Friend, nor did thy hand reach the hem of the Beloved. Marvel, then, at this, O ye endued with sight!

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای اهل ديار عشق ﴾ شمع باقی را ارياح فانی احاطه نموده و جمال غلام روحانی در غبار تيره ظلمانی مستور مانده * سلطان سلاطين عشق در دست رعايای ظلم مظلوم و حمامه قدسی در دست جغدان گرفتار * جميع اهل سرادق ابهی و ملأ اعلی نوحه و ندبه مينمايند و شما در کمال راحت در ارض غفلت اقامت نموده‌ايد و خود را هم از دوستان خالص محسوب داشته‌ايد * فباطل ما أنتم تظنّون *
paragraphs.translit: ay ahl-i diyār-i ʿishq! shamʿ-i bāqī rā aryāḥ-i fānī iḥāṭa namūda va jamāl-i ghulām-i rūḥānī dar ghubār-i tīra-yi ẓulmānī mastūr mānda. sulṭān-i salāṭīn-i ʿishq dar dast-i raʿāyā-yi ẓulm maẓlūm va ḥamāma-yi qudsī dar dast-i jughdān giriftār. jamīʿ-i ahl-i sarādiq-i abhā va malaʾ-i aʿlā nawḥa u nudba mī-namāyand va shumā dar kamāl-i rāḥat dar arḍ-i ghaflat iqāmat namūda-īd va khud rā ham az dūstān-i khāliṣ maḥsūb dāshta-īd. fa-bāṭil mā antum taẓunnūn.

i18n.en: O ye that dwell in the city of love! The everlasting candle is encompassed by the winds of mortality, and the beauty of the celestial Youth lieth hidden in murky, tenebrous dust. The King of the kings of love is oppressed at the hands of the subjects of tyranny, and the dove of holiness is held captive in the talons of owls. All that dwell in the Most Glorious Pavilion and the Concourse on high lament and mourn, while ye repose in utter ease upon the earth of heedlessness, and reckon yourselves among the sincere friends. Vain is that which ye imagine!

notes.official: *sarādiq-i abhā* ('the Most Glorious Pavilion'): *abhā*, the elative of the *b-h-y* 'glory' root, is again kept neutral ('Most Glorious'), the onomastic resonance with *Bahāʾ-Allāh* recorded as lexical fact only (cf. HWP-2, HWP-77). *ghulām-i rūḥānī* ('the celestial Youth') and *ḥamāma-yi qudsī* ('the dove of holiness') held captive 'in the talons of owls' render the lyric imagery literally.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای جهلای معروف بعلم ﴾ چرا در ظاهر دعوی شبانی کنيد و در باطن ذئب اغنام من شده‌ايد * مَثَل شما مثل ستاره قبل از صبح است که در ظاهر درّيّ و روشن است و در باطن سبب اضلال و هلاکت کاروانهای مدينه و ديار من است *
paragraphs.translit: ay juhalā-yi maʿrūf bi-ʿilm! chirā dar ẓāhir daʿvā-yi shabānī kunīd va dar bāṭin ẕiʾb-i aghnām-i man shuda-īd? mathal-i shumā mithl-i sitāra-yi qabl az ṣubḥ ast ki dar ẓāhir durrī u rawshan ast va dar bāṭin sabab-i iḍlāl u halākat-i kārvān-hā-yi madīna u diyār-i man ast.

i18n.en: O ye ignorant ones renowned for learning! Wherefore do ye, in outward seeming, lay claim to shepherding, while inwardly ye have become wolves unto My flock? Ye are like the star before the dawn, which in outward seeming is bright and shining, yet inwardly is the cause of the straying and perdition of the caravans of My city and My land.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای بظاهر آراسته و بباطن کاسته ﴾ مَثَلِ شما مثل آب تلخ صافی است که کمال لطافت و صفا از آن در ظاهر مشهود شود چون بدست صرّاف ذائقه احديّه افتد قطره ای از آن را قبول نفرمايد * بلی تجلّی آفتاب در تراب و مرآت هر دو موجود ولکن از فَرْقَدان تا ارض فرق دان بلکه فرق بی منتهی در ميان *
paragraphs.translit: ay bi-ẓāhir ārāsta va bi-bāṭin kāsta! mathal-i shumā mithl-i āb-i talkh-i ṣāfī ast ki kamāl-i laṭāfat u ṣafā az ān dar ẓāhir mashhūd shavad; chūn bi-dast-i ṣarrāf-i ẕāʾiqa-yi aḥadiyya uftad qaṭra-ī az ān rā qabūl nafarmāyad. balī, tajallī-yi āftāb dar turāb u mirʾāt har du mawjūd, va lākin az farqadān tā arḍ farq dān, balki farq-i bī-muntahā dar miyān.

i18n.en: O thou that art outwardly adorned but inwardly diminished! Thou art like a bitter water, clear to the eye, from which the utmost delicacy and purity appear in outward seeming; yet, should it fall into the hand of the Assayer of the taste of oneness, He would accept not a single drop thereof. Yea, the effulgence of the sun shineth alike upon the dust and the mirror, yet know the difference between them to be as great as from the Two Guardian-stars unto the earth — nay, an infinite difference lieth between.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای دوست لسانی من ﴾ قدری تأمّل اختيار کن هرگز شنيده ای که يار و اغيار در قلبی بگنجد؟ پس اغيار را بران تا جانان بمنزل خود در آيد *
paragraphs.translit: ay dūst-i lisānī-yi man! qadrī taʾammul ikhtiyār kun. hargiz shanīda-ī ki yār u aghyār dar qalbī bigunjad? pas aghyār rā birān tā jānān bi-manzil-i khud dar-āyad.

i18n.en: O My Friend in Word! Ponder a while. Hast thou ever heard that friend and stranger could be contained within one heart? Drive out, then, the stranger, that the Beloved may enter His own abode.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر خاک ﴾ جميع آنچه در آسمانها و زمين است برای تو مقرّر داشتم مگر قلوب را که محلّ نزول تجلّی جمال و اجلال خود معيّن فرمودم * و تو منزل و محلّ مرا بغير من گذاشتی چنانچه در هر زمان که ظهور قدس من آهنگ مکان خود نمود غير خود را يافت اغيار ديد و لا مکان بحرم جانان شتافت * و مع ذلک ستر نمودم و سرّ نگشودم و خجلت ترا نپسنديدم *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i khāk! jamīʿ-i ānchi dar āsmān-hā u zamīn ast barā-yi tu muqarrar dāshtam, magar qulūb rā ki maḥall-i nuzūl-i tajallī-yi jamāl u ijlāl-i khud muʿayyan farmūdam. va tu manzil u maḥall-i marā bi-ghayr-i man guẕāshtī, chunānchi dar har zamān ki ẓuhūr-i quds-i man āhang-i makān-i khud namūd ghayr-i khud rā yāft, aghyār dīd va lā-makān bi-ḥaram-i jānān shitāft. va maʿa ẕālik satr namūdam va sirr nagushūdam va khijlat-i turā napasandīdam.

i18n.en: O Son of Dust! All that is in the heavens and the earth have I ordained for thee, save the human heart, which I have made the seat of the descent of the effulgence of My beauty and glory; yet thou didst yield My home and dwelling unto another than Me, so that, whensoever the manifestation of My holiness sought its own abode, it found a stranger there, and, beholding the alien, it hastened, placeless, unto the sanctuary of the Beloved. Yet, notwithstanding, I veiled thy state and disclosed not the secret, and consented not unto thy shame.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای جوهر هوی ﴾ بسا سحرگاهان که از مشرق لا مکان بمکان تو آمدم و ترا در بستر راحت بغير خود مشغول يافتم و چون برق روحانی بغمام عزّ سلطانی رجوع نمودم و در مکامن قرب خود نزد جنود قدس اظهار نداشتم *
paragraphs.translit: ay jawhar-i havā! basā saḥargāhān ki az mashriq-i lā-makān bi-makān-i tu āmadam va turā dar bistar-i rāḥat bi-ghayr-i khud mashghūl yāftam, va chūn barq-i rūḥānī bi-ghamām-i ʿizz-i sulṭānī rujūʿ namūdam va dar makāmin-i qurb-i khud nazd-i junūd-i quds iẓhār nadāshtam.

i18n.en: O Essence of Passion! Many a dawn have I come from the dayspring of the Placeless unto thine abode, and found thee upon the couch of ease occupied with another than Me; whereupon, like a flash of spiritual lightning, I returned unto the clouds of the glory of sovereignty, and made it not manifest, there in the hidden retreats of My nearness, unto the hosts of holiness.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر جود ﴾ در باديه های عدم بودی و ترا بمدد تراب امر در عالم ملک ظاهر نمودم و جميع ذرّات ممکنات و حقائق کائنات را بر تربيت تو گماشتم چنانچه قبل از خروج از بطن امّ دو چشمه شير منير برای تو مقرّر داشتم و چشمها برای حفظ تو گماشتم و حبّ ترا در قلوب القا نمودم و بصرف جود ترا در ظلّ رحمتم پروردم و از جوهر فضل و رحمت ترا حفظ فرمودم * و مقصود از جميع اين مراتب آن بود که بجبروت باقی ما درآئی و قابل بخششهای غيبی ما شوی * و تو غافل چون بثمر آمدی از تمامی نعيمم غفلت نمودی و بگمان باطل خود پرداختی بقسمی که بالمرّه فراموش نمودی و از باب دوست بايوان دشمن مقرّ يافتی و مسکن نمودی*
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i jūd! dar bādiya-hā-yi ʿadam būdī va turā bi-madad-i turāb-i amr dar ʿālam-i mulk ẓāhir namūdam va jamīʿ-i ẕarrāt-i mumkināt u ḥaqāʾiq-i kāʾināt rā bar tarbiyat-i tu gumāshtam, chunānchi qabl az khurūj az baṭn-i umm du chashma-yi shīr-i munīr barā-yi tu muqarrar dāshtam va chashm-hā barā-yi ḥifẓ-i tu gumāshtam va ḥubb-i turā dar qulūb ilqā namūdam va bi-ṣirf-i jūd turā dar ẓill-i raḥmatam parvardam va az jawhar-i faḍl u raḥmat turā ḥifẓ farmūdam. va maqṣūd az jamīʿ-i īn marātib ān būd ki bi-jabarūt-i bāqī-yi mā dar-āʾī va qābil-i bakhshish-hā-yi ghaybī-yi mā shavī. va tu ghāfil chūn bi-thamar āmadī az tamāmī-yi naʿīmam ghaflat namūdī va bi-gumān-i bāṭil-i khud pardākhtī, bi-qismī ki bi-l-marra farāmūsh namūdī va az bāb-i dūst bi-aivān-i dushman maqarr yāftī va maskan namūdī.

i18n.en: O Son of Bounty! Out of the wastes of nothingness, with the clay of My command, I brought thee forth into the world of dominion, and appointed for thy training every atom of existence and the realities of all created things. Thus, ere thou camest forth from thy mother's womb, I ordained for thee two founts of gleaming milk, appointed eyes to watch over thee, and instilled the love of thee into [men's] hearts. Out of sheer bounty I nurtured thee beneath the shadow of My mercy, and guarded thee by the essence of My grace and lovingkindness. And My purpose in all this was that thou mightest enter Our everlasting realm of omnipotence and become worthy of Our unseen gifts. Yet thou, heedless, when thou didst come to ripeness, didst neglect all My bounties and busy thyself with thine own vain fancy, so that thou didst utterly forget, and, turning from the door of the Friend, didst find thy seat and take up thine abode within the palace of the enemy.

notes.official: Two glossary fields converge. *turāb-i amr* ('the clay of My command') takes *amr* in its command / creative-fiat register, not the technical Bahá'í 'Cause': the clause describes the raising of the human from non-being (*bādiya-hā-yi ʿadam*, 'the wastes of nothingness') by divine decree — see the extended *amr* entry, which confirms that none of the Part II occurrences bears the settled 'the Cause' sense. *ʿālam-i mulk* ('the world of dominion,' *mulk* = the created material realm) and *jabarūt-i bāqī* ('Our everlasting realm of omnipotence,' *jabarūt*) hold the realm-hierarchy mapping fixed in Part I: *mulk* 'dominion,' *malakūt* 'kingdom,' *jabarūt* 'realm of omnipotence.'

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای بنده دنيا ﴾ در سحرگاهان نسيم عنايت من بر تو مرور نمود و ترا در فراش غفلت خفته يافت و بر حال تو گريست و باز گشت *
paragraphs.translit: ay banda-yi dunyā! dar saḥargāhān nasīm-i ʿināyat-i man bar tu murūr namūd va turā dar firāsh-i ghaflat khufta yāft va bar ḥāl-i tu girīst va bāz gasht.

i18n.en: O Bondslave of the World! Many a dawn hath the breeze of My lovingkindness passed over thee and found thee slumbering upon the couch of heedlessness; whereupon it wept over thy plight and returned.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر ارض ﴾ اگر مرا خواهی جز مرا مخواه و اگر اراده جمالم داری چشم از عالميان بردار زيرا که اراده من و غير من چون آب و آتش در يک دل و قلب نگنجد *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i arḍ! agar marā khvāhī juz marā makhvāh, va agar irāda-yi jamālam dārī chashm az ʿālamiyān bardār, zīrā ki irāda-yi man u ghayr-i man chūn āb u ātish dar yak dil u qalb naganjad.

i18n.en: O Son of Earth! Wouldst thou have Me, seek none but Me; and wouldst thou behold My beauty, close thine eyes to the world; for My will and the will of another can no more be contained within one heart than can water and fire.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای بيگانهء با يگانه ﴾ شمع دلت برافروخته دست قدرت منست آن را ببادهای مخالف نفس و هوی خاموش مکن و طبيب جميع علّتهای تو ذکر منست فراموشش منما * حبّ مرا سرمايه خود کن و چون بصر و جان عزيزش دار*
paragraphs.translit: ay bīgāna-yi bā yagāna! shamʿ-i dilat barafrūkhta dast-i qudrat-i manast; ān rā bi-bād-hā-yi mukhālif-i nafs u havā khāmūsh makun, va ṭabīb-i jamīʿ-i ʿillat-hā-yi tu ẕikr-i manast, farāmūshash manamā. ḥubb-i marā sarmāya-yi khud kun va chūn baṣar u jān ʿazīzash dār.

i18n.en: O thou that art estranged from the One! The candle of thy heart is kindled by the hand of My power; quench it not with the contrary winds of self and passion. The healer of all thine ills is the remembrance of Me; forget it not. Make My love thy treasure, and cherish it as thy very sight and life.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای برادر من ﴾ از لسان شکرينم کلمات نازنينم شنو و از لب نمکينم سلسبيل قدس معنوی بياشام * يعنی تخمهای حکمت لدنّيم را در ارض طاهر قلب بيفشان و بآب يقين آبش ده تا سنبلات علم و حکمت من سر سبز از بلده طيّبه انبات نمايد *
paragraphs.translit: ay birādar-i man! az lisān-i shakarīnam kalimāt-i nāzanīnam shinaw va az lab-i namakīnam salsabīl-i quds-i maʿnavī biyāshām. yaʿnī tukhm-hā-yi ḥikmat-i ladunnīyam rā dar arḍ-i ṭāhir-i qalb bīfshān va bi-āb-i yaqīn ābash dih tā sunbulāt-i ʿilm u ḥikmat-i man sar-sabz az balda-yi ṭayyiba inbāt namāyad.

i18n.en: O My Brother! Hearken to the delightsome words of My honeyed tongue, and quaff the stream of holiness and inner meaning from My sweet lips. That is: sow the seeds of My divinely-given wisdom in the pure soil of the heart, and water them with the water of certitude, that the hyacinths of My knowledge and wisdom may spring up verdant from the goodly city [of thy heart].

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای اهل رضوان من ﴾ نهال محبّت و دوستی شما را در روضه قدس رضوان بيد ملاطفت غرس نمودم و بنيسان مرحمت آبش دادم حال نزديک بثمر رسيده جهدی نمائيد تا محفوظ ماند و بنار امل و شهوت نسوزد *
paragraphs.translit: ay ahl-i riḍvān-i man! nihāl-i maḥabbat u dūstī-yi shumā rā dar rawḍa-yi quds-i riḍvān bi-yad-i mulāṭafat ghars namūdam va bi-nīsān-i marḥamat ābash dādam; ḥāl nazdīk bi-thamar rasīda, jahdī namāʾīd tā maḥfūẓ mānad va bi-nār-i amal u shahvat nasūzad.

i18n.en: O ye that dwell in My Paradise! With the hand of loving-kindness I have planted in the holy garden of Riḍván the young tree of your love and friendship, and watered it with the gentle showers of My tender mercy; now that it hath drawn near to its fruit-bearing, strive that it may be preserved, and be not consumed in the fire of craving and lust.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای دوستان من ﴾ سراج ضلالت را خاموش کنيد و مشاعل باقيهء هدايت در قلب و دل برافروزيد که عنقريب صرّافان وجود در پيشگاه حضور معبود جز تقوای خالص نپذيرند و غير عمل پاک قبول ننمايند *
paragraphs.translit: ay dūstān-i man! sirāj-i ḍalālat rā khāmūsh kunīd va mashāʿil-i bāqiya-yi hidāyat dar qalb u dil barafrūzīd, ki ʿan-qarīb ṣarrāfān-i vujūd dar pīshgāh-i ḥuḍūr-i maʿbūd juz taqvā-yi khāliṣ napaẕīrand va ghayr-i ʿamal-i pāk qabūl nanamāyand.

i18n.en: O My Friends! Put out the lamp of error, and kindle within your hearts the abiding torches of divine guidance; for erelong the assayers of mankind shall, in the sacred presence of the Adored One, accept naught but purest piety, and receive nothing but the deed unsullied.

paragraphs.fa:
﴿ ای پسر تراب ﴾ حکمای عباد آنانند که تا سمع نيابند لب نگشايند چنانچه ساقی تا طلب نبيند ساغر نبخشد و عاشق تا بجمال معشوق فائز نشود از جان نخروشد * پس بايد حبّه های حکمت و علم را در ارض طيّبه قلب مبذول داريد و مستور نمائيد تا سنبلات حکمت الهی از دِل برآيد نه از گِل *
(در سطر اوّل لوح مذکور و مسطورست و در سرادق حفظ اللّه مستور)
paragraphs.translit:
ay pisar-i turāb! ḥukamā-yi ʿibād ānanand ki tā samʿ nayāband lab nagushāyand, chunānchi sāqī tā ṭalab nabīnad sāghar nabakhshad va ʿāshiq tā bi-jamāl-i maʿshūq fāʾiz nashavad az jān nakhurūshad. pas bāyad ḥabba-hā-yi ḥikmat u ʿilm rā dar arḍ-i ṭayyiba-yi qalb mabẕūl dārīd va mastūr namāʾīd tā sunbulāt-i ḥikmat-i ilāhī az dil bar-āyad na az gil.
(dar saṭr-i avval-i lawḥ-i maẕkūr u masṭūrast va dar sarādiq-i ḥifẓ-i allāh mastūr.)

i18n.en: O Son of Dust! The wise are they that speak not until they gain a hearing, even as the cup-bearer proffereth not the cup until he seeth a seeker, and the lover crieth not out from the depths of his soul until he beholdeth the beauty of the beloved. Sow ye, then, the grains of wisdom and knowledge in the goodly soil of the heart, and keep them hidden, that the hyacinths of divine wisdom may spring forth from the heart and not from the mire. (This standeth written and recorded in the first line of the aforementioned Tablet, and lieth hidden within the pavilion of the safekeeping of God.)

notes.official: The signature wordplay of the Part: *sunbulāt-i ḥikmat-i ilāhī az dil bar-āyad na az gil* — 'that the hyacinths of divine wisdom may spring forth from the *dil* (heart, دِل) and not from the *gil* (mire, گِل).' The two words are a near-minimal pair (*d* / *g*), and the figure turns the agricultural image (seed sown in soil) back upon itself: true wisdom grows from the heart, not from mere clay. Rendered 'from the heart and not from the mire,' preserving the antithesis.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای بنده من ﴾ ملک بی زوال را بانزالی از دست منه و شاهنشهی فردوس را بشهوتی از دست مده * اينست کوثر حيوان که از معين قلم رحمن ساری گشته طوبی للشّاربين *
paragraphs.translit: ay banda-yi man! mulk-i bī-zavāl rā bi-inzālī az dast maneh va shāhanshahī-yi firdaws rā bi-shahvatī az dast madih. īnast kawthar-i ḥayavān ki az maʿīn-i qalam-i raḥmān sārī gashta; ṭūbā li-sh-shāribīn.

i18n.en: O My Servant! Let not the imperishable dominion go from thy hand for a fleeting shower [of gain], and cast not away the sovereignty of Paradise for a lust. This is the Kawthar of life that hath flowed from the wellspring of the Pen of the All-Merciful. Blessed are they that drink!

notes.official: *mulk-i bī-zavāl rā bi-inzālī az dast maneh* — a lexical crux. *inzāl* (√n-z-l, 'a sending-down, a downpour') stands parallel to *bi-shahvatī* ('for a lust') in the next clause, so functionally 'for some trifling, transient thing.' Rendered 'for a fleeting shower [of gain],' with the interpolation bracketed; the literal 'a mere sending-down' and the idiomatic 'a paltry thing' are the alternatives. *mulk-i bī-zavāl* ('the imperishable dominion,' *mulk*) holds the realm mapping. The closing *kawthar-i ḥayavān* ('the Kawthar of life') names the paradisal river/fountain of Qur'an 108:1.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر روح ﴾ قفس بشکن و چون همای عشق بهوای قدس پرواز کن و از نَفْس بگذر و با نَفَس رحمانی در فضای قدس ربّانی بيارام *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i rūḥ! qafas bishkan va chūn humā-yi ʿishq bi-havā-yi quds parvāz kun va az nafs biguẕar va bā nafas-i raḥmānī dar faḍā-yi quds-i rabbānī biyārām.

i18n.en: O Son of the Spirit! Burst thy cage, and, like the Humá-bird of love, soar into the air of holiness. Renounce self, and, with the breath of the All-Merciful, repose in the divine expanse of holiness.

notes.official: The wordplay *nafs* / *nafas*: 'renounce *nafs* (self, the ego-soul, نفْس) and, with the *nafas-i raḥmānī* (the breath of the All-Merciful, نفَس), repose…' — one consonantal skeleton (نفس), two words divided by vocalization. The *Nafas al-Raḥmān*, the 'Breath of the Compassionate' from which the cosmos is exhaled, is Ibn ʿArabī's technical term (cf. the *ʿamāʾ* / primal-Cloud note in Part I). Rendered 'renounce self … with the breath of the All-Merciful,' preserving the figure. *humā-yi ʿishq* ('the Humá-bird of love') retains *Humá* as a proper name — the fortune-bestowing bird of Persian lore — kept distinct from *ʿanqā* 'phoenix' (HWP-1); see the bestiary entry.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر رماد ﴾ براحت يومی قانع مشو و از راحت بيزوال باقيه مگذر و گلشن باقی عيش جاودان را بگلخن فانی ترابی تبديل منما * از زندان بصحراهای خوش جان عروج کن و از قفس امکان برضوان دلکش لامکان بخرام *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i ramād! bi-rāḥat-i yawmī qāniʿ mashaw va az rāḥat-i bī-zavāl-i bāqiya maguẕar va gulshan-i bāqī-yi ʿaysh-i jāvidān rā bi-gulkhan-i fānī-yi turābī tabdīl manamā. az zindān bi-ṣaḥrā-hā-yi khush-i jān ʿurūj kun va az qafas-i imkān bi-riḍvān-i dilkash-i lā-makān bikhrām.

i18n.en: O Son of Ashes! Be not content with the ease of a day, and forgo not the imperishable rest that abideth. Barter not the everlasting rose-garden of eternal delight for the perishing ash-pit of dust. Rise from thy prison unto the fair meadows of the soul, and from the cage of contingency wing thy flight to the heart-ravishing Riḍván of the Placeless.

notes.official: The wordplay *gulshan* / *gulkhan*: 'barter not the *gulshan* (rose-garden, گلشن) of eternal delight for the *gulkhan* (the ash-pit / bath-house stoke-hole, گلخن) of dust.' The paired compounds — *gul-shan* 'rose-bower' against *gul-khan* 'furnace' — turn on a single consonant, opposing the garden of paradise to the ash-heap of the world. *pisar-i ramād* ('O Son of Ashes') keeps *ramād* 'ashes' distinct from the *khāk* / *turāb* 'dust' field. *riḍvān* (the paradise-garden, and the name of its keeper-angel) is retained.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای بنده من ﴾ از بند ملک خود را رهائی بخش و از حبس نفس خود را آزاد کن وقت را غنيمت شمر زيرا که اين وقت را ديگر نبينی و اين زمان را هرگز نيابی *
paragraphs.translit: ay banda-yi man! az band-i mulk khud rā rahāʾī bakhsh va az ḥabs-i nafs khud rā āzād kun; vaqt rā ghanīmat shumar, zīrā ki īn vaqt rā dīgar nabīnī va īn zamān rā hargiz nayābī.

i18n.en: O My Servant! Free thyself from the fetters of [worldly] dominion, and release thy soul from the prison of self. Seize thy chance, for it will come to thee no more: this very time thou shalt not see again, this moment thou shalt never find anew.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای فرزند کنيز من ﴾ اگر سلطنت باقی بينی البتّه بکمال جدّ از ملک فانی درگذری و لکن ستر آنرا حکمتهاست و جلوه اين را رمزها جز افئده پاک ادراک ننمايد *
paragraphs.translit: ay farzand-i kanīz-i man! agar salṭanat-i bāqī bīnī al-batta bi-kamāl-i jidd az mulk-i fānī dar-guẕarī, va lākin satr-i ānrā ḥikmat-hāst va jilva-yi īnrā rumūz; juz afʾida-yi pāk idrāk nanamāyad.

i18n.en: O Son of My Handmaid! Couldst thou but behold the everlasting sovereignty, thou wouldst surely, with all thy might, pass beyond this fleeting dominion. Yet in the veiling of the one lie manifold wisdoms, and in the unveiling of the other manifold mysteries, which none but the pure of heart can comprehend.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای بنده من ﴾ دل را از غلّ پاک کن و بی حسد ببساط قدس احد بخرام *
paragraphs.translit: ay banda-yi man! dil rā az ghill pāk kun va bī ḥasad bi-bisāṭ-i quds-i aḥad bikhrām.

i18n.en: O My Servant! Cleanse thy heart of rancour, and, void of envy, stride into the sacred court of the One.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای دوستان من ﴾ در سبيل رضای دوست مشی نمائيد و رضای او در خلق او بوده و خواهد بود * يعنی دوست بی رضای دوست خود در بيت او وارد نشود و در اموال او تصرّف ننمايد و رضای خود را بر رضای او ترجيح ندهد و خود را در هيچ امری مقدّم نشمارد * فتفکّروا فی ذلک يا اولی الافکار*
paragraphs.translit: ay dūstān-i man! dar sabīl-i riḍā-yi dūst mashī namāʾīd, va riḍā-yi ū dar khalq-i ū būda va khvāhad būd. yaʿnī dūst bī riḍā-yi dūst-i khud dar bayt-i ū vārid nashavad va dar amvāl-i ū taṣarruf nanamāyad va riḍā-yi khud rā bar riḍā-yi ū tarjīḥ nadihad va khud rā dar hīch amrī muqaddam nashumārad. fa-tafakkarū fī ẕālika yā ulī l-afkār.

i18n.en: O My Friends! Walk ye in the path of the Friend's good-pleasure, and know that His good-pleasure lieth in the good-pleasure of His creatures. That is: no friend shall enter the house of his friend save with his friend's consent, nor lay hands upon his goods, nor prefer his own will to his friend's, nor in any matter account himself above him. Reflect ye upon this, O ye endued with thought!

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای رفيق عرشی ﴾ بد مشنو و بد مبين و خود را ذليل مکن و عويل برميار * يعنی بد مگو تا نشنوی و عيب مردم را بزرگ مدان تا عيب تو بزرگ ننمايد و ذلّت نفسی مپسند تا ذلّت تو چهره نگشايد * پس با دل پاک و قلب طاهر و صدر مقدّس و خاطر منزّه در ايّام عمر خود که اقلّ از آنی محسوبست فارغ باش تا بفراغت از اين جسد فانی بفردوس معانی راجع شوی و در ملکوت باقی مقرّ يابی *
paragraphs.translit: ay rafīq-i ʿarshī! bad mashnaw va bad mabīn va khud rā ẕalīl makun va ʿavīl barmayār. yaʿnī bad magū tā nashnavī va ʿayb-i mardum rā buzurg madān tā ʿayb-i tu buzurg nanamāyad va ẕillat-i nafsī mapasand tā ẕillat-i tu chihra nagushāyad. pas bā dil-i pāk u qalb-i ṭāhir u ṣadr-i muqaddas u khāṭir-i munazzah dar ayyām-i ʿumr-i khud ki aqall az ānī maḥsūbast fārigh bāsh, tā bi-farāghat az īn jasad-i fānī bi-firdaws-i maʿānī rājiʿ shavī va dar malakūt-i bāqī maqarr yābī.

i18n.en: O Companion of the Throne! Hear no evil, and see no evil; abase not thyself, neither wail and lament. That is: speak no evil, that thou mayest hear none; and magnify not the faults of others, that thine own faults may not appear great; and desire not the abasement of any soul, that thine own abasement be not laid bare. Live, then, with a pure heart, a stainless mind, a sanctified breast, and an unsullied thought, throughout the days of thy life — which are reckoned less than a fleeting moment — that, freed from this mortal frame, thou mayest wing thy way unto the paradise of inner meanings and take thine abode in the everlasting kingdom.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ وای وای ای عاشقان هوای نفسانی ﴾ از معشوق روحانی چون برق گذشته‌ايد و بخيال شيطانی دل محکم بسته‌ايد * ساجد خياليد و اسم آن را حقّ گذاشته‌ايد و ناظر خاريد و نام آن را گل گذارده‌ايد * نه نَفَس فارغی از شما برآمد و نه نسيم انقطاعی از رياض قلوبتان وزيد * نصايح مشفقه محبوبرا بباد داده‌ايد و از صفحه دل محو نموده‌ايد و چون بهآئم در سبزه زار شهوت و امل تعيّش مينمائيد*
paragraphs.translit: vāy vāy, ay ʿāshiqān-i havā-yi nafsānī! az maʿshūq-i rūḥānī chūn barq guẕashta-īd va bi-khayāl-i shayṭānī dil muḥkam basta-īd. sājid-i khayālīd va ism-i ān rā ḥaqq guẕāshta-īd va nāẓir-i khārīd va nām-i ān rā gul guẕārda-īd. na nafas-i fārighī az shumā bar-āmad va na nasīm-i inqiṭāʿī az riyāḍ-i qulūbatān vazīd. naṣāʾiḥ-i mushfiqa-yi maḥbūb rā bi-bād dāda-īd va az ṣafḥa-yi dil maḥv namūda-īd va chūn bahāʾim dar sabza-zār-i shahvat u amal taʿayyush mī-namāʾīd.

i18n.en: Woe, woe, O ye lovers of carnal desire! Like lightning ye have passed the spiritual Beloved by, and have set your hearts fast upon a satanic fancy. Ye bow down before an idol of imagination and have named it Truth; ye gaze upon a thorn and have called it a rose. Not one free breath hath risen from you, nor hath the breeze of detachment blown from the gardens of your hearts. The loving counsels of the Well-Beloved ye have flung to the winds and effaced from the tablet of your hearts; and, like the beasts of the field, ye graze and take your fill in the meadow of lust and craving.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای برادران طريق ﴾ چرا از ذکر نگار غافل گشته‌ايد و از قرب حضرت يار دور مانده‌ايد ؟ صِرْف جمال در سرادق بيمثال بر عرش جلال مستوی و شما بهوای خود بجدال مشغول گشته‌ايد * روايح قدس ميوزد و نسائم جود در هبوب و کلّ بزکام مبتلی شده‌ايد و از جميع محروم مانده‌ايد * زهی حسرت بر شما و علی الّذين هم يمشون علی أعقابکم و علی أثر أقدامکم هم يمرّون *
paragraphs.translit: ay birādarān-i ṭarīq! chirā az ẕikr-i nigār ghāfil gashta-īd va az qurb-i ḥaḍrat-i yār dūr mānda-īd? ṣirf-i jamāl dar sarādiq-i bī-mithāl bar ʿarsh-i jalāl mustavī va shumā bi-havā-yi khud bi-jadāl mashghūl gashta-īd. ravāʾiḥ-i quds mī-vazad va nasāʾim-i jūd dar hubūb, va kull bi-zukām mubtalī shuda-īd va az jamīʿ maḥrūm mānda-īd. zih-i ḥasrat bar shumā va ʿalā lladhīna hum yamshūna ʿalā aʿqābikum va ʿalā athar-i aqdāmikum hum yamurrūn.

i18n.en: O Brethren of the Path! Wherefore have ye grown heedless of the remembrance of the Loved One, and remained afar from His presence? The very Essence of Beauty is seated upon the throne of majesty within the peerless pavilion, while ye are busied with your own vain contentions. The fragrances of holiness are wafting, and the breezes of bounty are blowing, yet ye are all stricken as with a rheum and remain shut out from them all. Alas for you, and for them that walk in your footsteps and tread in the traces of your feet!

paragraphs.fa:
﴿ ای پسران آمال ﴾ جامه غرور را از تن بر آريد و ثوب تکبّر از بدن بيندازيد *
(در سطر سيّم از اسطر قدس که در لوح ياقوتی از قلم خفی ثبت شده اين است )
paragraphs.translit:
ay pisarān-i āmāl! jāma-yi ghurūr rā az tan bar-ārīd va thawb-i takabbur az badan bīndāzīd.
(dar saṭr-i siyyum az asṭur-i quds ki dar lawḥ-i yāqūtī az qalam-i khafī thabt shuda īn ast.)

i18n.en: O Sons of Vain Desire! Strip off the garment of vainglory, and cast away the raiment of pride. (In the third line of the lines of holiness that is inscribed by the hidden Pen upon the ruby Tablet, this is [what is set down]:)

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای برادران ﴾ با يکديگر مدارا نمائيد و از دنيا دل برداريد بعزّت افتخار منمائيد و از ذلّت ننگ مداريد * قسم بجمالم که کلّ را از تراب خلق نمودم و البتّه بخاک راجع فرمايم *
paragraphs.translit: ay birādarān! bā yak-dīgar mudārā namāʾīd va az dunyā dil bardārīd; bi-ʿizzat iftikhār manamāʾīd va az ẕillat nang madārīd. qasam bi-jamālam ki kull rā az turāb khalq namūdam va al-batta bi-khāk rājiʿ farmāyam.

i18n.en: O Brethren! Be forbearing one with another, and set not your hearts on the things of this world. Glory not in honour, and be not ashamed of abasement. By My beauty! I have created all from dust, and unto dust will I surely cause them to return.

notes.official: The verse sets the two dust-words in deliberate parallel: *kull rā az turāb khalq namūdam va … bi-khāk rājiʿ farmāyam* — 'I have created all from *turāb* (dust), and unto *khāk* (dust) will I cause them to return.' The Arabic loan *turāb* (the creation-dust of Qur'an 3:59; 22:5; 30:20) and the Persian *khāk* are used interchangeably for stylistic variation, which is the philological ground for levelling both to 'Dust' in the vocative series rather than distinguishing them (see the vocative entry and HWP-5).

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسران تراب ﴾ اغنيا را از ناله سحرگاهی فقرا اخبار کنيد که مبادا از غفلت بهلاکت افتند و از سدره دولت بی نصيب مانند * الکرم و الجود من خصالی فهنيئا لمن تزيّن بخصالی *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisarān-i turāb! aghniyā rā az nāla-yi saḥargāhī-yi fuqarā akhbār kunīd ki mabādā az ghaflat bi-halākat uftand va az sidra-yi dawlat bī naṣīb mānand. al-karamu wa-l-jūdu min khiṣālī, fa-hanīʾan li-man tazayyana bi-khiṣālī.

i18n.en: O Sons of Dust! Tell the rich of the midnight sighing of the poor, lest heedlessness lead them into perdition and deprive them of the Tree of wealth. Bounty and generosity are of My attributes; well is it with him that adorneth himself with My virtues.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای ساذج هوی ﴾ حرص را بايد گذاشت و بقناعت قانع شد * زيرا که لازال حريص محروم بوده و قانع محبوب و مقبول *
paragraphs.translit: ay sāẕij-i havā! ḥirṣ rā bāyad guẕāsht va bi-qanāʿat qāniʿ shud, zīrā ki lā-zāl ḥarīṣ maḥrūm būda va qāniʿ maḥbūb u maqbūl.

i18n.en: O thou Simpleton of Passion! Greed must be forsaken, and one must rest content with contentment; for ever hath the greedy been deprived, and the contented beloved and approved.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر کنيز من ﴾ در فقر اضطراب نشايد و در غنا اطمينان نبايد * هر فقری را غنا در پی و هر غنا را فنا از عقب و لکن فقر از ماسوی اللّه نعمتی است بزرگ حقير مشماريد زيرا که در غايت آن غنای باللّه رخ بگشايد * و در اين مقام ( أنتم الفقرآء ) مستور و کلمه مبارکه ( و اللّه هو الغنيّ ) چون صبح صادق از افق قلب عاشق ظاهر و باهر و هويدا و آشکار شود و بر عرش غنا متمکّن گردد و مقرّ يابد *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i kanīz-i man! dar faqr iḍṭirāb nashāyad va dar ghinā iṭmīnān nabāyad. har faqrī rā ghinā dar pay va har ghinā rā fanā az ʿaqab, va lākin faqr az mā-sivā llāh niʿmatī ast buzurg, ḥaqīr mashumārīd, zīrā ki dar ghāyat-i ān ghinā-yi bi-llāh rukh bigushāyad. va dar īn maqām (antumu l-fuqarāʾ) mastūr va kalima-yi mubāraka (wa-llāhu huwa l-ghaniyy) chūn ṣubḥ-i ṣādiq az ufuq-i qalb-i ʿāshiq ẓāhir u bāhir u huvaydā u āshkār shavad va bar ʿarsh-i ghinā mutamakkin gardad va maqarr yābad.

i18n.en: O Son of My Handmaid! In poverty there should be no disquiet, and in wealth no repose. Every poverty is followed by wealth, and every wealth is followed by ruin; yet poverty in all save God is a mighty bounty — deem it not mean, for at its uttermost the wealth that is in God shall unveil its face. And in this station lieth hidden [the word] "ye are the poor," and the blessed word "and God is the All-Possessing" shall, like the true dawn, break forth resplendent, radiant, evident, and manifest from the horizon of the lover's heart, and shall be established upon the throne of wealth and there abide.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسران غفلت و هوی ﴾ دشمن مرا در خانه من راه داده‌ايد و دوست مرا از خود رانده‌ايد چنانچه حبّ غير مرا در دل منزل داده‌ايد * بشنويد بيان دوست را و برضوانش اقبال نمائيد * دوستان ظاهر نظر بمصلحت خود يکديگر را دوست داشته و دارند و لکن دوست معنوی شما را لاجل شما دوست داشته و دارد بلکه مخصوص هدايت شما بلايای لا تحصی قبول فرموده * بچنين دوست جفا مکنيد و بکويش بشتابيد * اينست شمس کلمه صدق و وفا که از افق اصبع مالک اسماء اشراق فرموده * افتحوا آذانکم لاصغاء کلمة اللّه المهيمن القيّوم *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisarān-i ghaflat u havā! dushman-i marā dar khāna-yi man rāh dāda-īd va dūst-i marā az khud rānda-īd, chunānchi ḥubb-i ghayr-i marā dar dil manzil dāda-īd. bishnavīd bayān-i dūst rā va bi-riḍvānash iqbāl namāʾīd. dūstān-i ẓāhir naẓar bi-maṣlaḥat-i khud yak-dīgar rā dūst dāshta va dārand, va lākin dūst-i maʿnavī shumā rā li-ajl-i shumā dūst dāshta va dārad, balki makhṣūṣ-i hidāyat-i shumā balāyā-yi lā tuḥṣā qabūl farmūda. bi-chunīn dūst jafā makunīd va bi-kūyash bishitābīd. īnast shams-i kalima-yi ṣidq u vafā ki az ufuq-i iṣbaʿ-i mālik-i asmāʾ ishrāq farmūda. iftaḥū āẕānakum li-iṣghāʾi kalimati llāhi l-muhaymini l-qayyūm.

i18n.en: O Sons of Heedlessness and Passion! Ye have let My enemy into My house and driven My friend from you, for ye have lodged the love of another than Me within your hearts. Hearken to the words of the Friend, and turn toward His paradise. Friends in the world's eyes love one another for their own advantage; but the true Friend hath loved and doth love you for your own sakes — nay, for the sake of your guidance He hath borne afflictions beyond all reckoning. Be not faithless to such a Friend; hasten, rather, unto His street. This is the sun of the word of truth and faithfulness, that hath dawned from the horizon of the finger of the Lord of Names. Open your ears to hearken unto the word of God, the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting.

notes.official: Two Qur'anic phrases are embedded and set off as quotations: *antumu l-fuqarāʾ* ('ye are the poor') and *wa-llāhu huwa l-ghaniyy* ('and God is the All-Possessing'), from Qur'an 35:15 (*yā ayyuhā n-nāsu antumu l-fuqarāʾu ilā llāhi wa-llāhu huwa l-ghaniyyu l-ḥamīd*). Rendered literally and kept as quotations; *faqr* ('poverty') and *ghinā* ('wealth, self-sufficiency') are the mystical poverty/riches pair — *faqr min mā-sivā llāh*, 'poverty in all save God,' being the Sufi ideal of absolute dependence upon God.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای مغروران باموال فانيه ﴾ بدانيد که غنا سدّيست محکم ميان طالب و مطلوب و عاشق و معشوق * هرگز غنی بر مقرّ قرب وارد نشود و بمدينه رضا و تسليم در نيايد مگر قليلی * پس نيکوست حال آن غنی که غنا از ملکوت جاودانی منعش ننمايد و از دولت ابدی محرومش نگرداند * قسم باسم اعظم که نور آن غنی اهل آسمان را روشنی بخشد چنانچه شمس اهل زمين را *
paragraphs.translit: ay maghrūrān bi-amvāl-i fāniya! bidānīd ki ghinā saddī-st muḥkam miyān-i ṭālib u maṭlūb u ʿāshiq u maʿshūq. hargiz ghanī bar maqarr-i qurb vārid nashavad va bi-madīna-yi riḍā u taslīm dar-nayāyad magar qalīlī. pas nīkūst ḥāl-i ān ghanī ki ghinā az malakūt-i jāvidānī manʿash nanamāyad va az dawlat-i abadī maḥrūmash nagardānad. qasam bi-ism-i aʿẓam ki nūr-i ān ghanī ahl-i āsmān rā rawshanī bakhshad chunānchi shams ahl-i zamīn rā.

i18n.en: O ye that pride yourselves on perishable riches! Know that wealth is a mighty barrier between the seeker and the sought, between the lover and the beloved. Never shall the rich attain the seat of nearness, nor enter the city of contentment and submission — save a few. Well is it, then, with that rich one whom his riches hinder not from the eternal kingdom, nor deprive of the everlasting dominion. By the Most Great Name! The splendour of such a rich one shall give light to the dwellers of heaven, even as the sun giveth light to the people of the earth.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای اغنيای ارض ﴾ فقرا امانت منند در ميان شما * پس امانت مرا درست حفظ نمائيد و براحت نفس خود تمام نپردازيد *
paragraphs.translit: ay aghniyā-yi arḍ! fuqarā amānat-i manand dar miyān-i shumā. pas amānat-i marā durust ḥifẓ namāʾīd va bi-rāḥat-i nafs-i khud tamām napardāzīd.

i18n.en: O Ye Rich Ones of the Earth! The poor are My trust among you; guard, then, My trust well, and be not wholly occupied with your own ease.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای فرزند هوی ﴾ از آلايش غنا پاک شو و با کمال آسايش در افلاک فقر قدم گذار تا خمر بقا از عين فنا بياشامی *
paragraphs.translit: ay farzand-i havā! az ālāyish-i ghinā pāk shaw va bā kamāl-i āsāyish dar aflāk-i faqr qadam guẕār tā khamr-i baqā az ʿayn-i fanā biyāshāmī.

i18n.en: O Son of Passion! Cleanse thyself from the defilement of riches, and with perfect serenity set foot within the heavens of poverty, that from the wellspring of annihilation thou mayest quaff the wine of everlastingness.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر من ﴾ صحبت اشرار غم بيفزايد و مصاحبت ابرار زنگ دل بزدايد * من أراد ان يأنس مع اللّه فليأنس مع احبّائه و من أراد ان يسمع کلام اللّه فليسمع کلمات اصفيائه *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i man! ṣuḥbat-i ashrār gham bīfzāyad va muṣāḥabat-i abrār zang-i dil bizdāyad. man arāda an yaʾnisa maʿa llāhi fa-l-yaʾnis maʿa aḥibbāʾihi, va man arāda an yasmaʿa kalāma llāhi fa-l-yasmaʿ kalimāti aṣfiyāʾihi.

i18n.en: O My Son! The company of the wicked increaseth grief, while fellowship with the righteous scoureth the rust from the heart. Whoso would commune with God, let him commune with His loved ones; and whoso would hearken to the word of God, let him hearken to the words of His chosen ones.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ زينهار ای پسر خاک ﴾ با اشرار الفت مگير و مؤانست مجو که مجالست اشرار نور جان را بنار حسبان تبديل نمايد *
paragraphs.translit: zīnhār ay pisar-i khāk! bā ashrār ulfat magīr va muʾānasat majū, ki mujālasat-i ashrār nūr-i jān rā bi-nār-i ḥusbān tabdīl namāyad.

i18n.en: Beware, O Son of Dust! Consort not with the wicked, and seek not their fellowship; for the company of the wicked turneth the light of the soul into the fire of perdition.

notes.official: *nār-i ḥusbān* ('the fire of perdition'): *ḥusbān* (√ḥ-s-b, 'reckoning, calculation; a visitation, a thunderbolt') carries the Qur'anic sense of a chastisement sent down (cf. *ḥusbānan mina s-samāʾ*, 'a reckoning from heaven,' Qur'an 18:40). Rendered 'the fire of perdition,' with 'the fire of [divine] reckoning' the alternative. *pisar-i khāk* keeps the levelled 'Dust.'

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر کنيز من ﴾ اگر فيض روح القدس طلبی با احرار مصاحب شو * زيرا که ابرار جام باقی از کف ساقی خلد نوشيده‌اند و قلب مردگان را چون صبح صادق زنده و منير و روشن نمايند *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i kanīz-i man! agar fayḍ-i rūḥu l-qudus ṭalabī bā aḥrār muṣāḥib shaw, zīrā ki abrār jām-i bāqī az kaff-i sāqī-yi khuld nūshīda-and va qalb-i murdagān rā chūn ṣubḥ-i ṣādiq zinda u munīr u rawshan namāyand.

i18n.en: O Son of My Handmaid! Wouldst thou seek the grace of the Holy Spirit, enter into fellowship with the righteous; for they have drunk the everlasting cup from the hand of the immortal Cup-Bearer, and, like the true dawn, they quicken, illumine, and make radiant the hearts of the dead.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای غافلان ﴾ گمان مبريد که اسرار قلوب مستور است بلکه بيقين بدانيد که بخطّ جلی مسطور گشته و در پيشگاه حضور مشهود *
paragraphs.translit: ay ghāfilān! gumān mabarīd ki asrār-i qulūb mastūr ast, balki bi-yaqīn bidānīd ki bi-khaṭṭ-i jalī masṭūr gashta va dar pīshgāh-i ḥuḍūr mashhūd.

i18n.en: O ye Heedless Ones! Think not that the secrets of hearts are hidden; nay, know ye of a certainty that they are inscribed in plain characters and lie open before the [divine] Presence.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای دوستان ﴾ براستی ميگويم که جميع آنچه در قلوب مستور نموده‌ايد نزد ما چون روز واضح و ظاهر و هويداست و لکن ستر آنرا سبب جود و فضل ماست نه استحقاق شما *
paragraphs.translit: ay dūstān! bi-rāstī mī-gūyam ki jamīʿ-i ānchi dar qulūb mastūr namūda-īd nazd-i mā chūn rūz vāḍiḥ u ẓāhir u huvaydāst, va lākin satr-i ānrā sabab-i jūd u faḍl-i māst na istiḥqāq-i shumā.

i18n.en: O Friends! Verily I say, whatsoever ye have hidden within your hearts is unto Us open and manifest as the day; yet the veiling thereof is by reason of Our bounty and grace, and not through any merit of yours.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر انسان ﴾ شبنمی از ژرف دريای رحمت خود بر عالميان مبذول داشتم و احدی را مقبل نيافتم * زيرا که کلّ از خمر باقی لطيف توحيد بماء کثيف نبيد اقبال نموده‌اند و از کأس جمال باقی بجام فانی قانع شده‌اند * فبئس ما هُم به يقنعون *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i insān! shabnamī az zharf-i daryā-yi raḥmat-i khud bar ʿālamiyān mabẕūl dāshtam va aḥadī rā muqbil nayāftam, zīrā ki kull az khamr-i bāqī-yi laṭīf-i tawḥīd bi-māʾ-i kathīf-i nabīdh iqbāl namūda-and va az kaʾs-i jamāl-i bāqī bi-jām-i fānī qāniʿ shuda-and. fa-biʾsa mā hum bihi yaqnaʿūn.

i18n.en: O Son of Man! A dewdrop from the fathomless ocean of My mercy I shed upon the peoples of the world, yet found none turning thereunto; for every one hath turned away from the choice, celestial wine of the Divine Unity unto the foul water of dregs, and, contenting himself with the perishing cup, hath cast away the chalice of abiding beauty. Vile is that wherewith they are content!

notes.official: *pisar-i insān*, 'O Son of Man.' Persian here uses *insān* — the human being as such, the intimate knower — rendered 'Man,' consistent with the Part I mapping (*insān* = 'Man'; the mortal-fleshly *bashar* = 'Mortal Man'). *bashar* does not occur in the Part II vocatives. The *khamr … tawḥīd* ('the wine of the Divine Unity') against *māʾ … nabīdh* ('the water of dregs') renders the sobriety/intoxication figure literally.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر خاک ﴾ از خمر بی مثال محبوب لا يزال چشم مپوش و بخمر کدره فانيه چشم مگشا * از دست ساقی احديّه کأوس باقيه برگير تا همه هوش شوی و از سروش غيب معنوی شنوی * بگو ای پست فطرتان از شراب باقی قدسم چرا بآب فانی رجوع نموديد *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i khāk! az khamr-i bī-mithāl-i maḥbūb-i lā-yazāl chashm mapūsh va bi-khamr-i kadira-yi fāniya chashm magushā. az dast-i sāqī-yi aḥadiyya kaʾūs-i bāqiya bar-gīr tā hama hūsh shavī va az surūsh-i ghayb-i maʿnavī shanavī. bi-gū: ay past-fiṭratān! az sharāb-i bāqī-yi qudsam chirā bi-āb-i fānī rujūʿ namūdīd?

i18n.en: O Son of Dust! Close not thine eyes to the matchless wine of the everlasting Beloved, and open them not unto the turbid and perishing wine. Take from the hand of the Cup-Bearer of oneness the cups of abiding life, that thou mayest become all awareness, and mayest hearken to the mystic voice of the hidden Realm of inner meaning. Say: O ye base of nature! Wherefore have ye turned from My holy and abiding wine unto perishing water?

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ بگو ای اهل ارض ﴾ براستی بدانيد که بلای ناگهانی شما را در پی است و عقاب عظيمی از عقب * گمان مبريد که آنچه را مرتکب شديد از نظر محو شده * قسم بجمالم که در الواح زبرجدی از قلم جلی جميع اعمال شما ثبت گشته *
paragraphs.translit: bi-gū: ay ahl-i arḍ! bi-rāstī bidānīd ki balā-yi nāgahānī shumā rā dar pay ast va ʿiqāb-i ʿaẓīmī az ʿaqab. gumān mabarīd ki ānchi rā murtakib shudīd az naẓar maḥv shuda. qasam bi-jamālam ki dar alvāḥ-i zabarjadī az qalam-i jalī jamīʿ-i aʿmāl-i shumā thabt gashta.

i18n.en: Say: O ye People of the Earth! Know of a certainty that a sudden calamity followeth in your wake, and that a grievous chastisement pursueth you from behind. Deem not that what ye have committed hath been blotted from My sight. By My beauty! All your deeds hath My clear Pen inscribed upon tablets of chrysolite.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای ظالمان ارض ﴾ از ظلم دست خود را کوتاه نمائيد که قسم ياد نموده‌ام از ظلم احدی نگذرم و اين عهدی است که در لوح محفوظ محتوم داشتم و بخاتم عزّ مختوم *
paragraphs.translit: ay ẓālimān-i arḍ! az ẓulm dast-i khud rā kūtāh namāʾīd, ki qasam yād namūda-am az ẓulm-i aḥadī naguẕaram; va īn ʿahdī ast ki dar lawḥ-i maḥfūẓ maḥtūm dāshtam va bi-khātam-i ʿizz makhtūm.

i18n.en: O ye Oppressors of the Earth! Withdraw your hands from tyranny, for I have vowed not to overlook the injustice of any man. This is My covenant, which I have irrevocably decreed in the Preserved Tablet and sealed with the seal of glory.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای عاصيان ﴾ بردباری من شما را جری نمود و صبر من شما را بغفلت آورد که در سبيلهای مهلک خطرناک بر مراکب نار نفس بی باک ميرانيد گويا مرا غافل شمرده‌ايد و يا بی خبر انگاشته‌ايد *
paragraphs.translit: ay ʿāṣiyān! burdbārī-yi man shumā rā jarī namūd va ṣabr-i man shumā rā bi-ghaflat āvard, ki dar sabīl-hā-yi muhlik-i khaṭarnāk bar marākib-i nār-i nafs bī-bāk mī-rānīd; gūyā marā ghāfil shumarda-īd va yā bī-khabar angāshta-īd.

i18n.en: O ye Transgressors! My long-suffering hath emboldened you, and My patience hath made you heedless, so that ye urge on, in the perilous and deadly ways, the steeds of the fire of self, all recklessly — as though ye had reckoned Me heedless, or accounted Me unaware.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای مهاجران ﴾ لسان مخصوص ذکر منست بغيبت ميالائيد و اگر نفس ناری غلبه نمايد بذکر عيوب خود مشغول شويد نه بغيبت خلق من * زيرا که هر کدام از شما بنفس خود اَبصَر و اعرفيد از نفوس عباد من *
paragraphs.translit: ay muhājirān! lisān makhṣūṣ-i ẕikr-i manast, bi-ghībat mayālāʾīd; va agar nafs-i nārī ghalaba namāyad, bi-ẕikr-i ʿuyūb-i khud mashghūl shavīd na bi-ghībat-i khalq-i man, zīrā ki har kudām az shumā bi-nafs-i khud abṣar u aʿrafīd az nufūs-i ʿibād-i man.

i18n.en: O ye Emigrants! The tongue is set apart for My remembrance; defile it not with backbiting. Should the fiery self prevail over you, busy yourselves with the mention of your own faults, and not with the backbiting of My servants; for each of you knoweth his own self better and more truly than the selves of My servants.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسران وهم ﴾ بدانيد چون صبح نورانی از افق قدس صمدانی بردمد البتّه اسرار و اعمال شيطانی که در ليل ظلمانی معمول شده ظاهر شود و بر عالميان هويدا گردد *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisarān-i vahm! bidānīd chūn ṣubḥ-i nūrānī az ufuq-i quds-i ṣamadānī bar-damad, al-batta asrār u aʿmāl-i shayṭānī ki dar layl-i ẓulmānī maʿmūl shuda ẓāhir shavad va bar ʿālamiyān huvaydā gardad.

i18n.en: O Sons of Fancy! Know that when the luminous morn breaketh from the horizon of everlasting holiness, then surely shall the satanic secrets and deeds, wrought in the darkness of night, be laid bare and made manifest before the peoples of the world.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای گياه خاک ﴾ چگونه است که با دست آلوده بشکر مباشرت جامه خود ننمائی و با دل آلوده بکثافت شهوت و هوی معاشرتم را جوئی و بممالک قدسم راه خواهی ؟ هيهات هيهات عمّا أنتم تريدون *
paragraphs.translit: ay giyāh-i khāk! chigūna ast ki bā dast-i ālūda bi-shakar mubāsharat-i jāma-yi khud nanamāʾī va bā dil-i ālūda bi-kathāfat-i shahvat u havā muʿāsharatam rā jūʾī va bi-mamālik-i qudsam rāh khvāhī? hayhāt hayhāt ʿammā antum turīdūn.

i18n.en: O Herb of the Earth! How is it that thou, who wouldst not touch thy garment with a hand made sticky with sugar, dost yet seek My fellowship with a heart defiled by the filth of lust and passion, and dost desire to enter My hallowed realms? Far, far from that which ye desire!

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسران آدم ﴾ کلمه طيّبه و اعمال طاهره مقدّسه بسمآء عزّ احديّه صعود نمايد * جهد کنيد تا اعمال از غبار ريا و کدورت نفس و هوی پاک شود و بساحت عزّ قبول درآيد * چه که عنقريب صرّافان وجود در پيشگاه حضور معبود جز تقوای خالص نپذيرند و غير عمل پاک قبول ننمايند * اينست آفتاب حکمت و معانی که از افق فم مشيّت ربّانی اشراق فرمود طوبی للمقبلين *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisarān-i ādam! kalima-yi ṭayyiba va aʿmāl-i ṭāhira-yi muqaddasa bi-samāʾ-i ʿizz-i aḥadiyya ṣuʿūd namāyad. jahd kunīd tā aʿmāl az ghubār-i riyāʾ u kudūrat-i nafs u havā pāk shavad va bi-sāḥat-i ʿizz-i qabūl dar-āyad. chi ki ʿan-qarīb ṣarrāfān-i vujūd dar pīshgāh-i ḥuḍūr-i maʿbūd juz taqvā-yi khāliṣ napaẕīrand va ghayr-i ʿamal-i pāk qabūl nanamāyand. īnast āftāb-i ḥikmat u maʿānī ki az ufuq-i fam-i mashiyyat-i rabbānī ishrāq farmūd; ṭūbā li-l-muqbilīn.

i18n.en: O Sons of Adam! Goodly words and pure and holy deeds ascend unto the heaven of the glory of the Divine Oneness. Strive that your deeds may be cleansed from the dust of hypocrisy and the murkiness of self and passion, and may find favour at the court of glory; for erelong the assayers of mankind shall, in the sacred presence of the Adored One, accept naught but purest piety and receive nothing but the deed unsullied. This is the sun of wisdom and inner meaning that hath shone from the horizon of the mouth of the divine Will. Blessed are they that turn thereunto!

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر عيش ﴾ خوش ساحتی است ساحت هستی اگر اندر آئی و نيکو بساطی است بساط باقی اگر از ملک فانی برتر خرامی و مليح است نشاط مستی اگر ساغر معانی از يد غلام الهی بياشامی * اگر باين مراتب فائز شوی از نيستی و فنا و محنت و خطا فارغ گردی *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i ʿaysh! khush sāḥatī-st sāḥat-i hastī agar andar-āyī, va nīkū bisāṭī-st bisāṭ-i bāqī agar az mulk-i fānī bartar khirāmī, va malīḥ ast nishāṭ-i mastī agar sāghar-i maʿānī az yad-i ghulām-i ilāhī biyāshāmī. agar bi-īn marātib fāʾiz shavī az nīstī u fanā u miḥnat u khaṭā fārigh gardī.

i18n.en: O Son of Joy! How fair is the realm of being, if thou wouldst but enter it! And how goodly is the carpet of everlastingness, if thou wouldst but stride beyond the perishing dominion! And how sweet is the rapture of ecstasy, if thou wouldst but drink the goblet of inner meaning from the hand of the celestial Youth! Shouldst thou attain these stations, thou wouldst be freed from nothingness and annihilation, from tribulation and error.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای دوستان من ﴾ ياد آوريد آن عهدی را که در جبل فاران که در بقعه مبارکه زمان واقع شده با من نموده‌ايد و ملأ اعلی و اصحاب مدين بقا را بر آن عهد گواه گرفتم و حال احديرا بر آن عهد قائم نمی بينم البتّه غرور و نافرمانی آن را از قلوب محو نموده بقسميکه اثری از آن باقی نمانده و من دانسته صبر نمودم و اظهار نداشتم *
paragraphs.translit: ay dūstān-i man! yād āvarīd ān ʿahdī rā ki dar jabal-i fārān ki dar buqʿa-yi mubāraka-yi zamān vāqiʿ shuda bā man namūda-īd, va malaʾ-i aʿlā va aṣḥāb-i madyan-i baqā rā bar ān ʿahd gavāh giriftam, va ḥāl aḥadī rā bar ān ʿahd qāʾim namī-bīnam. al-batta ghurūr u nā-farmānī ān rā az qulūb maḥv namūda, bi-qismī ki atharī az ān bāqī namānda; va man dānista ṣabr namūdam va iẓhār nadāshtam.

i18n.en: O My Friends! Call ye to mind that covenant ye entered into with Me upon Mount Párán, situate within the blessed precinct of Time, wherein I took to witness the Concourse on high and the companions of the Midian of eternity; yet now I find none faithful unto that covenant. Verily, pride and rebellion have so effaced it from your hearts that no trace thereof remaineth. Yet, knowing this, I have been patient and disclosed it not.

notes.official: The covenant aphorism is sited in Mosaic-Sinai geography. *jabal-i Fārān* is rendered 'Mount Párán' — Paran, the peak from which, with Sinai and Seir, the divine glory 'shone forth' (Deuteronomy 33:2; Habakkuk 3:3); *aṣḥāb-i Madyan*, 'the companions of Midian,' the region of Moses's exile and his covenant with Jethro (Exodus 2-3). *buqʿa mubāraka* ('the blessed spot/precinct') is itself the Qur'anic Sinai phrase — *al-buqʿa al-mubāraka* of Qur'an 28:30, the 'blessed spot' of the burning-bush theophany. The crux is *zamān*: it can be read as a place-name ('the blessed precincts of Zamán,' as the draft first had it) or as the common noun زمان 'time.' No Sinai toponym 'Zamān' is attested, and the plain lexical sense is 'time'; accuracy-first therefore prefers 'the blessed precinct of Time,' reading the site of the primordial covenant as a metaphysical locus (the pre-eternal covenant of *alastu bi-rabbikum*, Qur'an 7:172) rather than an unattested geographic name — a rendering that also keeps the WoH text independent of the authorised translation. The named-locus reading is recorded as the alternative in the overlay Sinai-toponym entry. These toponyms invite comparative-tradition commentary in the wiki; the surface text renders the geography literally without arguing it.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای بنده من ﴾ مثل تو مثل سيف پر جوهری است که در غلاف تيره پنهان باشد و باين سبب قدر آن بر جوهريان مستور ماند * پس از غلاف نفس و هوی بيرون آی تا جوهر تو بر عالميان هويدا و روشن آيد *
paragraphs.translit: ay banda-yi man! mithl-i tu mithl-i sayf-i pur-jawharī ast ki dar ghilāf-i tīra pinhān bāshad va bi-īn sabab qadr-i ān bar jawhariyān mastūr mānad. pas az ghilāf-i nafs u havā bīrūn āy tā jawhar-i tu bar ʿālamiyān huvaydā u rawshan āyad.

i18n.en: O My Servant! Thou art even as a finely tempered sword concealed in a darksome sheath, whereby its worth is hidden from the knowledge of jewellers. Come forth, then, from the sheath of self and passion, that thy worth may be made resplendent and manifest unto all the world.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای دوست من ﴾ تو شمس سمآء قدس منی خود را بکسوف دنيا ميالای * حجاب غفلت را خرق کن تا بی پرده و حجاب از خلف سحاب بدر آئی و جميع موجودات را بخلعت هستی بيارائی *
paragraphs.translit: ay dūst-i man! tu shams-i samāʾ-i quds-i manī, khud rā bi-kusūf-i dunyā mayālāy. ḥijāb-i ghaflat rā khirq kun tā bī parda u ḥijāb az khalf-i saḥāb badar āyī va jamīʿ-i mawjūdāt rā bi-khilʿat-i hastī biyārāyī.

i18n.en: O My Friend! Thou art the sun of the heaven of My holiness; let not the eclipse of the world darken thee. Rend asunder the veil of heedlessness, that from behind the clouds thou mayest come forth unveiled and unconcealed, and mayest adorn all created things with the robe of being.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای ابنآء غرور ﴾ بسلطنت فانيه ايّامی از جبروت باقی من گذشته و خود را باسباب زرد و سرخ می آرائيد و بدين سبب افتخار مينمائيد * قسم بجمالم که جميع را در خيمه يکرنگ تراب درآورم و همه اين رنگهای مختلفه را از ميان بردارم مگر کسانيکه برنگ من درآيند و آن تقديس از همهء رنگها است *
paragraphs.translit: ay abnāʾ-i ghurūr! bi-salṭanat-i fāniya-yi ayyāmī az jabarūt-i bāqī-yi man guẕashta va khud rā bi-asbāb-i zard u surkh mī-ārāʾīd va bi-dīn sabab iftikhār mī-namāʾīd. qasam bi-jamālam ki jamīʿ rā dar khayma-yi yak-rang-i turāb dar-āvaram va hama-yi īn rang-hā-yi mukhtalifa rā az miyān bardāram, magar kasānī ki bi-rang-i man dar-āyand, va ān taqdīs az hama-yi rang-hāst.

i18n.en: O Sons of Vainglory! For a fleeting sovereignty of a few days ye have forsaken My imperishable realm of omnipotence, and deck yourselves out in trappings of yellow and red, and thereat ye glory. By My beauty! I shall gather all beneath the one-hued tent of dust, and shall wipe out all these diverse hues from among them — save those who take on My own hue, and that is sanctification from all hues.

notes.official: *jabarūt-i bāqī* ('My imperishable realm of omnipotence,' *jabarūt*) holds the realm mapping. The close turns on *rang* ('hue, colour'): God will gather all beneath the 'one-hued tent of dust' (*khayma-yi yak-rang-i turāb*) and efface the 'diverse hues' — save those who 'take on My own hue' (*bi-rang-i man dar-āyand*), which is 'sanctification from all hues.' The figure echoes the Qur'anic *ṣibghata llāh*, 'the dye of God … and who is fairer than God in dyeing?' (Qur'an 2:138). Rendered literally.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای ابنآء غفلت ﴾ بپادشاهی فانی دل مبنديد و مسرور مشويد * مثل شما مثل طير غافلی است که بر شاخه باغی در کمال اطمينان بسرايد و بغتةً صيّاد اجل او را بخاک اندازد ديگر از نغمه و هيکل و رنگ او اثری باقی نماند * پس پند گيريد ای بندگان هوی *
