paragraphs.translit: ay abnāʾ-i ghaflat! bi-pādishāhī-yi fānī dil mabandīd va masrūr mashavīd. mithl-i shumā mithl-i ṭayr-i ghāfilī ast ki bar shākha-yi bāghī dar kamāl-i iṭmīnān bisarāyad va baghtatan ṣayyād-i ajal ū rā bi-khāk andāzad; dīgar az naghma u haykal u rang-i ū atharī bāqī namānad. pas pand gīrīd ay bandagān-i havā.

i18n.en: O Sons of Heedlessness! Set not your hearts on a fleeting kingship, nor rejoice therein. Ye are like the heedless bird that singeth in fullest security upon a garden bough, till of a sudden the fowler Death casteth it to the dust, and no more remaineth any trace of its song, its form, or its hue. Take heed, then, O bondslaves of passion!

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای فرزند کنيز من ﴾ لا زال هدايت باقوال بوده و اين زمان بافعال گشته * يعنی بايد جميع افعال قدسی از هيکل انسانی ظاهر شود چه که در اقوال کلّ شريکند و لکن افعال پاک و مقدّس مخصوص دوستان ماست * پس بجان سعی نمائيد تا بافعال از جميع ناس ممتاز شويد * کذلک نصحناکم فی لوح قدس منير *
paragraphs.translit: ay farzand-i kanīz-i man! lā-zāl hidāyat bi-aqvāl būda va īn zamān bi-afʿāl gashta. yaʿnī bāyad jamīʿ-i afʿāl-i qudsī az haykal-i insānī ẓāhir shavad, chi ki dar aqvāl kull sharīkand va lākin afʿāl-i pāk u muqaddas makhṣūṣ-i dūstān-i māst. pas bi-jān saʿī namāʾīd tā bi-afʿāl az jamīʿ-i nās mumtāz shavīd. kaẕālika naṣaḥnākum fī lawḥ-i quds-i munīr.

i18n.en: O Son of My Handmaid! Guidance hath ever been given by words, but now it is given by deeds. That is: all holy deeds must appear from the temple of man; for in words all have their share, but pure and holy deeds are the peculiar treasure of Our loved ones. Strive, then, with heart and soul, to be distinguished, by your deeds, from all mankind. Thus do We counsel you in a holy and shining Tablet.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر انصاف ﴾ در ليل جمال هيکل بقا از عقبه زمرّدی وفا بسدره منتهی رجوع نمود و گريست گريستنی که جميع ملأ عالين و کروبين از ناله او گريستند * و بعد از سبب نوحه و ندبه استفسار شد مذکور داشت که حسب الأمر در عقبه وفا منتظر ماندم و رائحه وفا از اهل ارض نيافتم و بعد آهنگ رجوع نمودم ملحوظ افتاد که حمامات قدسی چند در دست کلاب ارض مبتلی شده‌اند * در اين وقت حوريّه الهی از قصر روحانی بی ستر و حجاب دويد و سؤال از اسامی ايشان نمود و جميع مذکور شد الّا اسمی از اسمآء * و چون اصرار رفت حرف اوّل اسم از لسان جاری شد اهل غرفات از مکامن عزّ خود بيرون دويدند و چون بحرف دوم رسيد جميع بر تراب ريختند * در آن وقت ندا از مکمن قرب رسيد زياده بر اين جايز نه * إنّا کنّا شهدآء علی ما فعلوا و حينئذٍ کانوا يفعلون *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i inṣāf! dar layl jamāl-i haykal-i baqā az ʿaqaba-yi zumurrudī-yi vafā bi-sidra-yi muntahā rujūʿ namūd va girīst, girīstanī ki jamīʿ-i malaʾ-i ʿālīn u karūbīn az nāla-yi ū girīstand. va baʿd, az sabab-i nawḥa u nudba istifsār shud; maẕkūr dāsht ki ḥasb al-amr dar ʿaqaba-yi vafā muntaẓir māndam va rāʾiḥa-yi vafā az ahl-i arḍ nayāftam va baʿd āhang-i rujūʿ namūdam; malḥūẓ uftād ki ḥamāmāt-i qudsī chand dar dast-i kilāb-i arḍ mubtalī shuda-and. dar īn vaqt ḥūriyya-yi ilāhī az qaṣr-i rūḥānī bī satr u ḥijāb davīd va suʾāl az asāmī-yi īshān namūd va jamīʿ maẕkūr shud illā ismī az asmāʾ. va chūn iṣrār raft ḥarf-i avval-i ism az lisān jārī shud, ahl-i ghurafāt az makāmin-i ʿizz-i khud bīrūn davīdand, va chūn bi-ḥarf-i duvvum rasīd jamīʿ bar turāb rīkhtand. dar ān vaqt nidā az makman-i qurb rasīd: ziyāda bar īn jāʾiz na. innā kunnā shuhadāʾa ʿalā mā faʿalū wa-ḥīnaʾiẕin kānū yafʿalūn.

i18n.en: O Son of Equity! In the night season the Beauty of the immortal Being repaired from the emerald height of faithfulness unto the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary, and wept with such a weeping that all the Concourse on high and the cherubim wailed at His lamenting. Whereupon there was inquired the cause of the wailing and lamentation, and He made answer: According to the [divine] command I waited, expectant, upon the height of faithfulness, yet caught not the fragrance of faithfulness from the dwellers of the earth; and when I made to return, lo, I beheld certain holy doves sore afflicted in the talons of the dogs of earth. Thereupon the Maid of heaven hastened forth, unveiled and unscreened, from her mystic mansion, and asked their names; and all were named save one, and when she pressed, the first letter of the name flowed from the tongue, whereupon the dwellers of the celestial chambers rushed forth from their glorious habitations; and when it reached the second letter, they all fell upon the dust. In that moment a voice was heard from the inmost shrine of nearness: "Thus far and no farther." Verily We bear witness unto that which they wrought, and are even now committing.

notes.official: The book's most elaborate aphorism, and the sharpest instance of the *b-h-y* onomastics handled neutrally since Part I. In a night-vision the *jamāl-i haykal-i baqā* ('the Beauty of the immortal Being') ascends from the 'emerald height of faithfulness' to the *Sidra-yi Muntahā* (the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary, Qur'an 53:14) and weeps; the *malaʾ-i ʿālīn* ('the Concourse on high') and *karūbīn* ('the cherubim,' the Hebrew *kĕrûbîm*) wail with Him. The *ḥūriyya-yi ilāhī* — 'the Maid of heaven,' the celestial feminine figure of Bahá'u'lláh's visionary writings — rushes forth unveiled and asks the names of the afflicted 'holy doves.' All are named save one; when its Name is pressed, *the first letter* draws the dwellers of the celestial chambers forth, and *the second letter* fells them to the dust. As lexical fact: the unspoken Name is *Bahāʾ* (بهاء), the author's own title, whose first two letters are *bāʾ* (ب) and *hāʾ* (ه) — the letter-by-letter naming enacts the Name B-H. Per the ratified Part I ruling on the *b-h-y* self-signature, the surface English keeps the neutral 'the first letter … the second letter' and does not annotate or surface the acrostic; the interpretive self-signature reading remains a lens-level, *speculative* matter escalated to the reviewer and is not committed as a glossary entry. Because HWP-77 is a more explicit acrostic than any Part I instance, the editor report asks the reviewer to confirm by name that the standing ruling extends to it. The closing Arabic — *innā kunnā shuhadāʾa ʿalā mā faʿalū…* — is rendered literally.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای فرزند کنيز من ﴾ از لسان رحمن سلسبيل معانی بنوش و از مشرق بيان سبحان اشراق انوار شمس تبيان من غير ستر و کتمان مشاهده نما * تخمهای حکمت لدنّيم را در ارض طاهر قلب بيفشان و بآب يقين آبش ده تا سنبلات علم و حکمت من سر سبز از بلده طيّبه انبات نمايد *
paragraphs.translit: ay farzand-i kanīz-i man! az lisān-i raḥmān salsabīl-i maʿānī binūsh va az mashriq-i bayān-i subḥān ishrāq-i anvār-i shams-i tibyān min ghayr-i satr u kitmān mushāhada namā. tukhm-hā-yi ḥikmat-i ladunnīyam rā dar arḍ-i ṭāhir-i qalb bīfshān va bi-āb-i yaqīn ābash dih tā sunbulāt-i ʿilm u ḥikmat-i man sar-sabz az balda-yi ṭayyiba inbāt namāyad.

i18n.en: O Son of My Handmaid! Drink from the tongue of the All-Merciful the stream of inner meaning, and behold, from the dayspring of the utterance of the All-Glorious, the unveiled and unconcealed effulgence of the lights of the Sun of exposition. Sow the seeds of My divinely-given wisdom in the pure soil of the heart, and water them with the water of certitude, that the hyacinths of My knowledge and wisdom may spring up verdant from the goodly city [of thy heart].

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای پسر هوی ﴾ تا کی در هوای نفسانی طيران نمائی ؟ پر عنايت فرمودم تا در هوای قدس معانی پرواز کنی نه در فضای وهم شيطانی * شانه مرحمت فرمودم تا گيسوی مشکينم شانه نمائی نه گلويم بخراشی *
paragraphs.translit: ay pisar-i havā! tā kay dar havā-yi nafsānī ṭayarān namāyī? par ʿināyat farmūdam tā dar havā-yi quds-i maʿānī parvāz kunī na dar faḍā-yi vahm-i shayṭānī. shāna marḥamat farmūdam tā gīsū-yi mushkīnam shāna namāyī na gulūyam bikhrāshī.

i18n.en: O Son of Passion! How long wilt thou soar in the realm of carnal desire? Wings have I bestowed on thee, that thou mightest wing thy flight in the air of the holiness of inner meanings, and not in the sphere of satanic fancy. A comb, too, have I graciously given thee, that thou mightest dress My musk-scented tresses, and not lacerate My throat.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای بندگان من ﴾ شما اشجار رضوان منيد بايد باثمار بديعه منيعه ظاهر شويد تا خود و ديگران از شما منتفع شوند * لذا بر کلّ لازم که بصنايع و اکتساب مشغول گردند * اينست اسباب غنا يا اولی الألباب و انّ الأمور معلّقة باسبابها و فضل اللّه يغنيکم بها * و اشجار بی ثمار لايق نار بوده و خواهد بود *
paragraphs.translit: ay bandagān-i man! shumā ashjār-i riḍvān-i manīd, bāyad bi-athmār-i badīʿa-yi manīʿa ẓāhir shavīd tā khud u dīgarān az shumā muntafiʿ shavand. liẕā bar kull lāzim ki bi-ṣanāyiʿ u iktisāb mashghūl gardand. īnast asbāb-i ghinā yā ulī l-albāb; wa-inna l-umūra muʿallaqatun bi-asbābihā, wa-faḍlu llāhi yughnīkum bihā. va ashjār-i bī thamār lāyiq-i nār būda va khvāhad būd.

i18n.en: O My Servants! Ye are the trees of My paradise; ye must needs bring forth goodly and wondrous fruits, that ye yourselves and others may profit therefrom. Wherefore it is incumbent on all to engage in crafts and trades; for this is the means of wealth, O ye endued with understanding. Verily, all affairs hang upon their causes, and the grace of God shall suffice you thereby. Trees that yield no fruit have been, and shall ever be, but fit for the fire.

notes.official: *al-umūr* in the embedded Arabic maxim *wa-inna l-umūra muʿallaqatun bi-asbābihā* ('verily, all affairs hang upon their causes') takes *amr* (pl. *umūr*) in its general 'affair, matter' register — the third register documented in the extended *amr* entry, alongside the command/decree sense (HWP-29, 77) and distinct from the technical 'Cause' of Part I, which does not occur in Part II. The counsel to 'engage in crafts and trades' (*ṣanāyiʿ u iktisāb*) as 'the means of wealth' is rendered literally; *ulī l-albāb* is 'ye endued with understanding' (Qur'anic).

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای بنده من ﴾ پست‌ترين ناس نفوسی هستند که بی ثمر در ارض ظاهرند و فی الحقيقه از اموات محسوبند بلکه اموات از آن نفوس معطّله مهمله ارجح عند اللّه مذکور *
paragraphs.translit: ay banda-yi man! past-tarīn-i nās nufūsī hastand ki bī thamar dar arḍ ẓāhirand va fi l-ḥaqīqa az amvāt maḥsūband, balki amvāt az ān nufūs-i muʿaṭṭala-yi muhmala arjaḥ ʿinda llāh maẕkūr.

i18n.en: O My Servant! The basest of men are they that bring forth no fruit upon the earth. Such men are verily accounted among the dead — nay, better in the sight of God are the dead than those idle and worthless souls.

paragraphs.fa: ﴿ ای بنده من ﴾ بهترين ناس آنانند که باقتراف تحصيل کنند و صرف خود و ذوی القربی نمايند حبّاً للّه ربّ العالمين *
paragraphs.translit: ay banda-yi man! bihtarīn-i nās ānanand ki bi-iqtirāf taḥṣīl kunand va ṣarf-i khud u ẕawi l-qurbā namāyand ḥubban li-llāhi rabbi l-ʿālamīn.

i18n.en: O My Servant! The best of men are they that earn a livelihood by their calling and spend it upon themselves and their kindred, for the love of God, the Lord of all worlds.

paragraphs.fa: عروس معانی بديعه که ورای پرده‌های بيان مستور و پنهان بود بعنايت الهی و الطاف ربّانی چون شعاع منير جمال دوست ظاهر و هويدا شد * شهادت ميدهم ای دوستان که نعمت تمام و حجّت کامل و برهان ظاهر و دليل ثابت آمد ديگر تا همّت شما از مراتب انقطاع چه ظاهر نمايد * کذلک تمّت النّعمة عليکم و علی من فی السّموات و الأرضين و الحمد للّه ربّ العالمين *
paragraphs.translit: ʿarūs-i maʿānī-yi badīʿa ki varā-yi parda-hā-yi bayān mastūr u pinhān būd, bi-ʿināyat-i ilāhī u alṭāf-i rabbānī chūn shuʿāʿ-i munīr-i jamāl-i dūst ẓāhir u huvaydā shud. shahādat mī-diham ay dūstān ki niʿmat tamām u ḥujjat kāmil u burhān ẓāhir u dalīl thābit āmad; dīgar tā himmat-i shumā az marātib-i inqiṭāʿ chi ẓāhir namāyad. kaẕālika tammati n-niʿmatu ʿalaykum wa-ʿalā man fi s-samāwāti wa-l-arḍīn, wa-l-ḥamdu li-llāhi rabbi l-ʿālamīn.

i18n.en: The peerless bride of inner meanings, that lay concealed and hidden behind the veils of utterance, hath, through divine grace and heavenly favours, been made manifest and revealed, even as the radiant beam of the Beloved's beauty. I bear witness, O friends, that the bounty is complete, the proof consummate, the demonstration made plain, and the testimony established. It now remaineth to be seen what your own endeavour, in the stages of detachment, will make manifest. Thus is the bounty consummated upon you and upon them that are in the heavens and on the earth. And praise be to God, the Lord of all worlds.
